These notes have an anticipated maturity date of November 5, 2031, and are issued under Registration Statement No. 333-284538. The notes represent unsecured obligations of GS Finance Corp., fully and unconditionally guaranteed by The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc., and are part of GS Finance Corp.'s Medium-Term Notes, Series F program. The underlying benchmark is the EURO STOXX 50 Index (Bloomberg ticker: "SX5E Index"). Pricing is expected on or about October 30, 2026, with the original issue date slated for November 4, 2026, and maturity on November 5, 2031. The automatic call feature stipulates that if, on the call observation date (expected November 5, 2027), the index closing value is equal to or exceeds the initial index value, the notes will be automatically called. Investors will then receive at least $1,190.00 per $1,000 principal on the call payment date (expected November 10, 2027). The filing clarifies that no further payments will be made post-call, and investors will not benefit from any subsequent index appreciation. If the notes are not called, three maturity scenarios apply: (i) if the final index value is above the initial index value, investors receive $1,000 plus a leveraged upside payment calculated as $1,000 multiplied by the 150.00% leverage factor and the index's percentage increase; (ii) if the final index value is at or below the initial index value but remains at or above the 80.00% downside threshold, investors receive $1,000; or (iii) if the final index value falls below the downside threshold, investors receive a payment based on the index performance factor, which could result in losing all or a significant portion of the principal. The estimated value range of $890 to $950 reflects an initial value below the $1,000 original issue price. Through the Free Writing Prospectus dated October 15, 2026, GS Finance Corp. disclosed principal-at-risk auto-callable structured notes linked to the EURO STOXX 50 Index, detailing call provisions, leverage, downside threshold, CUSIP, and an estimated value range below the issue price. title: German Exports Rebound amid Demand from the US, EU, and AI Buildout - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Germany’s exports increased in the first half of 2026 and are providing a modest boost to GDP growth in Europe’s largest economy, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Our economists forecast that real exports will grow at a “robust” rate of 3.5% in 2026 and 2.4% the following year. Recent export strength reflects resilient foreign demand alongside modest, productivity-driven improvements in competitiveness. Goldman Sachs Research expects German exports to increase, driven by revived trade with the US and the European Union, plus the global artificial intelligence (AI) buildout. “Taken together, we are more optimistic about German export performance than at the start of 2026,” writes Niklas Garnadt, an economist in Goldman Sachs Research, in a report. Strong export performance in the first half of 2026 is consistent with healthy foreign demand and a modest improvement in relative unit labor costs, driven by stronger productivity growth. Garnadt cautions that competition from Chinese exporters is expected to continue weighing on German exports in the medium term, especially in third markets. Still, the brighter outlook marks a shift for a sector that has been a drag on growth since the onset of the European energy crisis in 2022, writes Garnadt. Increases in relative unit labor costs and the real effective exchange rate have recently taken a toll on German competitiveness. The near-term outlook for exports has “improved materially,” Garnadt writes. Survey-based, forward-looking export indicators have risen to their highest levels since the start of the European energy crisis. Hard data show that foreign manufacturing sales have risen since the start of the year, alongside a recovery in real goods exports. Foreign orders have increased even more sharply. This suggests further export growth in the quarters to come, according to Goldman Sachs Research. In addition to improved competitiveness, German exports to the US are recovering from the decline triggered last year by US tariffs. While exports in the second quarter remained materially below pre-tariff levels, the shortfall peaked in the second half of 2025 and has narrowed since then, writes Garnadt. Recent monthly economic data point to further improvement in the third quarter. Trade with the EU is also rebounding after the slump that followed the energy crunch four years ago. “Since early 2025, EU trade has become a significant tailwind, reflected in rising manufacturing sales and orders,” writes Garnadt. Thanks to the development of AI infrastructure worldwide, German computer, electronics, and electrical equipment companies are making meaningful contributions to export growth. AI-exposed goods have materially outperformed total exported goods over the past year, according to Goldman Sachs Research There was also stronger growth in exports of chemicals and intermediate goods in the first half of 2026, perhaps reflecting precautionary purchases related to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz this year. Garnadt writes that this trend may partly reverse in the months to come. And Chinese competition will remain a challenge over the medium term. Even so, Garnadt points out that Germany’s surprisingly positive performance in the first half of 2026 shows a significant shift in the export sector following a long period of relative weakness. “Positive near-term indicators, productivity-driven competitiveness gains, stronger demand from Europe and the US, and spillovers from the global AI cycle point to healthy export growth ahead,” he writes. title: Parallel-Twin Adventure Motorcycles That Punch Above Their Weight - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update Adventure motorcycles rank high in desirability thanks to their go-anywhere versatility, but the segment has a catch. Over the past decade, ADVs have grown bigger, heavier and costlier, with many flagships now topping $20,000, and that leaves plenty of riders wondering whether they need all of it. Often, they don’t. That’s why parallel-twin ADVs have become a popular alternative, thanks to their lower prices and lighter, more manageable packaging. The obvious worry is what you give up in exchange, but a lower price doesn’t have to mean a compromise. The twelve motorcycles on this list pack hardware, performance or features you'd usually find in a higher class, or on a bike with a much bigger price tag. Entry-level adventure bikes tend to be single-cylinder affairs, so the CFMoto Ibex 450 stands out the moment you look at its spec sheet. Its 449cc parallel-twin makes 44 horsepower and 32.5 pound-feet of torque, and the 270-degree crankshaft keeps power delivery smooth and linear, something most thumpers in this class can't claim. It's light, too, at just 419 pounds, and the adjustable seat height of 31.5 to 32.3 inches makes it welcoming for shorter riders. What really lifts the Ibex above its price tag is the kit. CFMoto didn't cut corners on the suspension, fitting adjustable KYB units at both ends with 7.9 inches of travel at both ends, and it rides on 21-inch front and 18-inch rear tubeless spoked wheels, a setup usually reserved for pricier bikes. A 320 mm front disc with a four-piston caliper, dual-channel ABS, and a 5-inch TFT with Bluetooth round out the package. At $5,999, it undercuts the KTM 390 Adventure R by $1,700, which is hard to ignore for a first ADV. Kawasaki's ADV lineup has long had a gap between the Versys-X 300 and the KLR650, and the KLE500 fills it neatly with some real dirt credentials. Its 451cc parallel-twin, shared with the Ninja 500 and Eliminator, makes 51 horsepower and 31.7 pound-feet of torque, but the clever part is the chassis. The engine acts as a stressed member of a steel frame that Kawasaki says weighs just 41.8 pounds, which helps to keep the wet weight to 426 pounds. That build is paired with ingredients that matter on the trail. The long, narrow seat should make standing on the pegs off-road easy, and a 21-inch front wheel, an inverted fork, and hand guards make it ready for rougher roads. A three-way adjustable windshield takes care of highway duties, and the 4.2-gallon tank offers decent range. Starting at $6,599 (the SE is $7,499), the KLE500 is one of the cheapest ways to get an off-road-ready twin. The Honda NX500 is the safe bet on this list, and that's exactly its appeal. It is powered by a 471cc parallel-twin engine that produces about 47 horsepower and 31.8 pound-feet of torque, an engine Honda has used across its lineup for years, so reliability is a given. At 432 pounds wet with a 32.7-inch seat, it's also easy to handle. Hardware features include a 41 mm Showa inverted fork, a preload-adjustable monoshock, 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheels, and dual 296 mm front discs with ABS. Traction control and a TFT display with smartphone connectivity are standard. The NX500 is more road-biased than the rest of this list, but it makes up for it with efficiency. It has a fuel economy of 65 mpg, which, paired with a 4.7-gallon tank, should deliver a range of roughly about 300 miles. For $6,899, that is hard to find. The BMW F 450 GS is the brand's new entry-level GS. While it has not launched yet, BMW states the F 450 GS will reach dealers in Q1 2027. It brings an all-new 420cc parallel-twin making 48 horsepower and 32 pound-feet of torque. It is paired with a six-speed gearbox and sits in a new tubular-steel frame that uses the engine as a stressed member, which helps keep the claimed road-ready weight to around 392 pounds. Suspension duties are handled by a 43 mm KYB inverted fork and a KYB shock, both with 7.1 inches of travel, and the bike rolls on 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheels with Brembo brakes. Even the base model, priced at $6,995, gets Rain, Road and Enduro riding modes, ABS Pro, traction control and a 6.5-inch TFT. The $8,195 GS Trophy adds BMW's Easy Ride Clutch, adjustable suspension and a Rallye windshield, and still costs $496 more than the KTM 390 Adventure R. The Benelli TRK 702 X doesn't have the brand recognition of its Japanese and European rivals, but its numbers make it hard to ignore. Powering it is a 698 cc parallel-twin engine that produces 70 horsepower and 51.6 pound-feet of torque, which makes it one of the most powerful ADVs under $9,000. A six-speed gearbox sends power to the rear wheel. It isn't lightweight, tipping the scales at 489 pounds wet, but the 5.3-gallon tank gives it the range for long hauls. Hardware features include a 50 mm upside-down fork, an adjustable rear monoshock, and 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheels. Braking comes from dual 320 mm front discs with four-piston calipers. It also gets a 5-inch TFT display with Bluetooth connectivity and full LED lighting. At $8,999, it's $2,000 cheaper than the Yamaha Tenere 700 while making similar power. It's more of a gravel-road tourer than a trail bike, but the value is hard to ignore. If any bike on this list shows how quickly Chinese brands have caught up, it's the CFMoto Ibex 800 E. Its 799 cc parallel-twin is based on KTM's LC8c design from the 790 Adventure, and it makes 94 horsepower and 56.8 pound-feet of torque. A two-way quick shifter comes standard, and the steel trellis frame carries fully adjustable KYB suspension and 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheels, for a curb weight of 509 pounds. Tech is where the Ibex really stands out. CFMoto sells only the top E trim in the US, and it comes with an 8-inch touchscreen, a rear-facing radar for blind-spot monitoring, Bosch cornering ABS, and six ride modes, features flagship ADVs often charge extra for. It also gets a steering damper, which few rivals in this class offer. At $10,299, that's a lot of bike for the money, with the only catch being a smaller dealer network than the established brands. Honda took its time joining the middleweight ADV party, but Transalp has made up for it with one of the best do-it-all packages in the segment. Its 755 cc parallel-twin, shared with the CB750 Hornet, makes about 90 horsepower and 55 pound-feet of torque. That's within 10 horsepower of the $15,199 Africa Twin, and at 468 pounds, the Transalp weighs about 42 pounds less than that bike. For $10,199, it's a serious amount of performance. The latest update makes the Transalp more capable off the pavement. The six-speed gearbox now comes only with Honda's E-Clutch, which allows clutchless shifts and reduces the chance of stalling off-road. It gets fully adjustable suspension, and it rides on 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wire-spoke wheels with 8.2 inches of ground clearance. The 33.7-inch seat height keeps it approachable, while torque control, five riding modes, and a 5-inch TFT display with Honda RoadSync round out the tech. Add Honda’s reputation for reliability, and it’s a do-it-all middleweight that's hard to fault. Kove isn't a household name yet, but the 800X Pro is the kind of bike that gets people talking. Powering it is a 799cc parallel-twin, which produces 95 horsepower and 59 pound-feet of torque. What stands out most is the weight. Kove claims a curb weight of 408 pounds, which is remarkably light for a middleweight with this much power. The rest of the spec sheet reads like a rally bike. Fully adjustable KYB suspension at both ends works with 10.8 inches of ground clearance, and there's a steering damper, tubeless tires, and standard tire-pressure monitoring. The seat is a tall 34.5 inches, the wheelbase is 59.5 inches, and the tank holds 5 gallons. At $11,299, the Kove brings this rally-style hardware to a price well below most European middleweight ADVs. As a newer brand, it still has to prove long-term reliability and dealer support. The Suzuki V-Strom 800DE might be the most underrated middleweight adventure bike out there. Sure, it may not look as attractive on paper as its more adventure-ready rival. Compared to its rivals, the V-Strom 800DE doesn’t produce the most power and is on the heavier side, but it will win you over for other reasons. Think of this as a value-focused, off-road-capable adventure bike, and things start to make sense. The biggest advantage the V-Strom 800DE offers over most of its rivals is that it’s a Suzuki. This company is usually late to the party but likes to overbuild the engines for long-term dependability. Additionally, the engine is tuned for more tractable, usable torque, and the bike is well-prepared for adventure, with long-travel suspension and a 21-inch spoked front wheel. And a starting price of $11,799 means it also undercuts the competition. The standard Tenere 700 is a segment-defining ADV, but the World Raid takes things up a notch, offering long-distance adventure-touring capability seldom seen at this price point. Over the standard T7, this ADV gets more comfort-oriented ergonomics and a massive 6.1-gallon fuel tank, the largest in the segment, enabling a 300-mile range. Even the KYB suspension is beefed up, with nearly an inch more wheel travel on both ends. Underneath all that, the CP2 engine remains, offering excellent real-world performance and dependability. And it’s backed by advanced 6-axis IMU-enabled rider aids, including slide and brake control. Compared to rivals like the Triumph Tiger 900 Rally Pro, KTM 890 Adventure R, and BMW F 900 GS Adventure, it’s also considerably cheaper. We want to hear from you. title: BMW Motorrad Presents the New BMW F 450 RR. - BMW Group
content:
Juliane DreslerBMW Group
            

            Tel: +49-151-601-95733



              send an e-mail “What I particularly like about the new BMW F 450 RR is how
    light, direct, and precise it is to ride. To me, that’s exactly what
    a supersport motorcycle should be. It’s great fun on twisty roads
    and performs just as well on the racetrack. At the same time, it
    clearly carries the DNA of our RR models. For me, it’s the perfect
    entry into the world of BMW RR motorcycles.”
Markus Flasch, CEO BMW Motorrad The new BMW F 450 RR: A lightweight supersport bike for the 
48-hp class—developed for precise handling and an immediate
    racing feel on winding country roads and the racetrack.
The new BMW F 450 RR for the 48-hp class was developed as a
  standalone supersport bike within the BMW F 450 model family. The
  focus was on signature BMW riding pleasure, enabled by
  supersport-specific chassis and geometry engineering, rigorous weight
  optimization, and a powerful parallel-twin engine. Its design clearly
  follows the current design language of the S 1000 RR and visually
  underscores its dynamic ambitions. The silhouette consistently translates this ambition into RR design
  language: the pronounced nose-down, tail-up stance, the signature
  RR flyline, and the winglets create a powerful forward orientation.
  Asymmetrical side fairing panels, gills on the right side, and the
  split face add distinctive accents and underscore the standalone
  interpretation of RR DNA. The LED headlight with its
  signature RR daytime running light design defines the bike’s
  distinctive appearance. Smooth and characterful parallel-twin engine with a 135-degree
    crankpin offset for dynamic riding pleasure.
At the heart of the new BMW F 450 RR is the newly developed
  fuel-injected parallel-twin engine first used in the F 450 GS,
  together with a stainless-steel underfloor muffler. For use in the
  F 450 RR, it has been specifically tuned to meet the requirements of a
  supersport bike and gives the motorcycle a particularly distinctive
  sound. With an output of 35 kW (48 hp) at 8,750 rpm and maximum torque
  of 43 Nm at 6,750 rpm, the new F 450 RR delivers powerful acceleration
  and confident roll-on performance. As much as 80 percent of the
  available torque is already on tap at 3,000 rpm, providing strong
  propulsion from low engine speeds. High-tech materials and optimized
  internal friction make these performance figures possible from exactly
  420 cc. This makes the engine one of the most compact and powerful
  units in the A2 parallel-twin segment. It not only meets the stringent
  Euro 5+ requirements, but is also particularly efficient, with fuel
  consumption of just 3.8 liters per 100 km. With its 14-liter fuel
  tank, the F 450 RR achieves a range of more than 350 km. The service
  interval is the BMW Motorrad-standard 10,000 km. The crankshaft with a 135-degree crankpin offset and a balance shaft
  combine characterful power delivery with excellent refinement and low
  vibration. Magnesium covers for the clutch and transmission support
  weight optimization. Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) for a significant increase in operating
    and riding comfort.
The optional Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) engages the clutch
  according to engine speed, increasing comfort and control—especially
  in urban traffic, while maneuvering, on winding country roads, and
  during sporty riding. In combination with Shift Assistant Pro, it
  enables riding and shifting without manual clutch operation; the
  clutch lever remains available for deliberate rider input. For the BMW F 450 RR M Sport, the ERC is available ex-factory as part
  of the Innovation Package; it can be retrofitted to all other variants
  as an Original BMW Motorrad Accessory. During overrun, the clutch
  remains closed, preserving engine braking until shortly before the
  motorcycle comes to a stop. Only when idle speed is reached does the
  ERC open automatically, reliably preventing the engine from stalling. Six-speed transmission and left-side secondary drive. Shift
    Assistant Pro for fast upshifts and downshifts without operating the
      clutch.
The six-speed transmission transfers torque to the left-side
  secondary drive via an X-ring chain. For rapid upshifts and downshifts
  without operating the clutch, the new F 450 RR is equipped with Shift
  Assistant Pro in every equipment variant except the base model. It can
  be retrofitted to the base model. ABS Pro, DBC, DTC, and MSR, plus the “Rain,” “Road,” and
    “Race” riding modes as standard—delivering a high level of riding
    pleasure and safety.
The standard “Rain,” “Road,” and “Race” riding modes allow
  riders to tailor the new BMW F 450 RR to their
  individual preferences. ABS Pro, Dynamic Brake Control (DBC), Dynamic
  Traction Control (DTC), and engine drag torque control (MSR) are also standard. Chassis with a tubular steel space frame for high rigidity,
    robustness, and riding precision. Supersport-specific tuning and a
    short wheelbase for agile handling and high stability.
The new BMW F 450 RR also uses the newly developed
  BMW F 450 GS chassis concept as its technical foundation, with a setup
  tailored specifically to supersport use. The tuning focused on agile
  handling, precise feedback, and high stability on winding country
  roads and the racetrack. The tubular frame is made of welded steel
  tubes and forged components, with the parallel-twin engine integrated
  as a load-bearing element. Front wheel control via a KYB upside-down telescopic fork and
    rear wheel control via an aluminum hollow-cast double-sided swingarm
    with a KYB central spring strut.
At the front, a torsionally rigid 43 mm KYB upside-down
  telescopic fork controls the wheel. On the Sport suspension, the fork
  offers adjustable rebound and compression damping. At the rear, the wheel is guided by a closed, highly
  torsion-resistant yet lightweight hollow-cast aluminum double-sided
  swingarm. It is paired with a directly mounted KYB central spring
  strut with adjustable spring preload and rebound damping. Wheels and tires designed for dynamic riding pleasure.
The new BMW F 450 RR rides on lightweight yet robust
  cast-aluminum wheels. The supersport bike is fitted with tubeless
  tires measuring 110/70-17 at the front and 150/60-17 at the rear. Powerful braking system combined with BMW Motorrad ABS Pro for
    safe braking, even when leaned over. Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) and
    the dynamic brake light provide additional safety features.
At the front wheel of the new BMW F 450 RR, a floating
  single-disc brake with a Brembo four-piston monobloc fixed caliper and
  a 310 mm brake disc provides confident and efficient deceleration. At
  the rear, a single-disc brake with a floating ByBre single-piston
  caliper and a 240 mm disc is used. BMW Motorrad ABS Pro is standard on the new BMW F 450 RR. The system
  enables ABS-assisted braking when leaned over, increasing safety in
    corners. Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) enhances
  safety during braking in challenging situations by preventing
  unintended throttle application. The dynamic brake light effectively
  alerts following vehicles that the motorcycle ahead is slowing down. Sporty, active ergonomics and equipment for controlled,
    dynamic riding pleasure on winding country roads and the
      racetrack.
A carefully engineered ergonomic triangle and clip-on
  handlebars directly connected to the forged-aluminum triple clamp
  provide a sporty, dynamic riding position without losing sight of
  riding comfort. The bodywork and the 14-liter fuel tank beneath it are
  shaped for secure support and effective knee grip. The new BMW F 450 RR comes standard with a two-piece seat at a height
  of 790 mm, offering a balanced combination of comfort and a sporty,
  active seating position. Ergonomics can be customized with Original
  BMW Motorrad Accessories: the high Sport rider’s seat raises the
  seating position by 20 mm, while the low rider’s seat lowers it by
  15 mm. The gearshift lever, footbrake lever, and side stand are made
  of forged aluminum. The passenger footpeg brackets are bolted to the
  rear frame—an exceptional feature in this vehicle class. Reversible shift pattern for an extra dose of sportiness and a
    true racing feel.
For an extra dose of sportiness, the shift pattern can be
  reversed quickly and with minimal effort—ideal for racetrack use. Powerful LED headlight and LED lighting as standard.
    Connectivity with comprehensive information and functionality
    through a large, perfectly legible 6.5-inch TFT display. Practical
    USB-C port in the cockpit area.
The new BMW F 450 RR comes standard with an LED headlight
  featuring daytime running light LEDs and an iconic daytime running
  light signature inspired by the current generation of the S 1000 RR.
  The turn indicators and taillight of the new F 450 RR also use LED technology. The standard 6.5-inch TFT display on the new BMW F 450 RR offers a
  wide range of information, brilliant display quality, and intuitive
  operation at a premium level. The TFT display features the
  Pure Ride Screen. M Sport variants with Riding Modes Pro also offer
  three additional Sport screens with detailed information on DTC,
  braking force, and lean angle, as well as a lap timer function. Riders
  can also make phone calls, listen to music, and navigate conveniently
  while riding. Four attractive equipment variants for the new BMW F 450 RR. The new BMW F 450 RR is available in four equipment variants. The BMW F 450 RR Base is finished in Cosmic Black.
  Finished in Racing Red, the 
BMW F 450 RR Sport additionally features Shift
  Assistant Pro and the Sport suspension. The range-topping models are
    the BMW F 450 RR M Sport and the 
BMW F 450 RR M Sport with Innovation Package
  (including Easy Ride Clutch), in Snaefell white / M Motorsport,
  including Riding Modes Pro, Shift Assistant Pro, and the Sport
  suspension. Their white frame and rim stickers in M Motorsport colors
  create distinctive visual accents. Questions and Answers About the New BMW F 450 RR. The key questions about the new BMW F 450 RR—answered concisely with
  specific technical data. What is the BMW F 450 RR?
The BMW F 450 RR is a lightweight supersport bike for the
  48-hp class and the entry point into the world of BMW RR. It combines
  a 35 kW (48 hp) parallel-twin engine with supersport-specific chassis
  geometry, 17-inch wheels, and a ready-to-ride weight of 177 kg. It was
  developed for dynamic riding on winding country roads and for use on
  the racetrack. Who is the BMW F 450 RR designed for?
The BMW F 450 RR is aimed at riders looking for an accessible
  supersport bike with precise handling and moderate power. This
  includes A2 license holders as well as experienced motorcyclists who
  prefer a lightweight, direct motorcycle for winding country roads,
  everyday use, and their first or regular racetrack outings. Is the BMW F 450 RR suitable for an A2 license?
Yes. With 35 kW (48 hp), the BMW F 450 RR meets the maximum
  engine output permitted in Europe for the A2 license class. No
  subsequent power reduction is required. What distinguishes the BMW F 450 RR from the BMW F 450
  GS?The BMW F 450 RR uses the 420 cc parallel-twin engine
  familiar from the BMW F 450 GS, but is consistently tuned for
  supersport use. Key differences include chassis geometry, ergonomics,
  fairing, aerodynamics, 17-inch tires, and the sporty control strategy
  of the riding modes. The riding position is more front-wheel-oriented,
  and the shift pattern can be reversed for the racetrack. What are the output, torque, and weight of the BMW F 450
  RR?The parallel-twin engine produces 35 kW (48 hp) at 8,750
  rpm and develops maximum torque of 43 Nm at 6,750 rpm. As much as 80
  percent of maximum torque is already available at 3,000 rpm. The DIN
  ready-to-ride weight is 177 kg, or 178 kg with the Easy Ride Clutch. What is the effect of the parallel-twin engine’s 135-degree
    crankpin offset?
The 135-degree crankpin offset creates uneven firing
  intervals, shaping the engine’s power delivery and sound. Together
  with the counter-rotating balance shaft, this crankshaft design
  combines characterful power delivery with excellent refinement and low vibration. How does the Easy Ride Clutch on the BMW F 450 RR work?
The Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) uses a centrifugal unit that
  automatically engages the clutch according to engine speed. In
  combination with Shift Assistant Pro, the rider does not need to
  operate the clutch manually during regular riding. The clutch lever
  remains available for deliberate rider input. During overrun, the ERC
  stays closed, preserving engine braking until shortly before the
  motorcycle comes to a stop; at idle speed, it opens automatically and
  prevents the engine from stalling. Is the Easy Ride Clutch standard, and can it be
      retrofitted?
The Easy Ride Clutch is included on the BMW F 450 RR M Sport
  with Innovation Package. It is available for the other variants as a
  retrofittable Original BMW Motorrad Accessory. With ERC, the
  ready-to-ride weight increases by one kilogram to 178 kg. Which riding modes and assistance systems are standard?
The BMW F 450 RR comes standard with the “Rain,” “Road,” and
  “Race” riding modes. Standard equipment also includes BMW Motorrad ABS
  Pro for lean-angle-optimized braking, Dynamic Brake Control (DBC),
  Dynamic Traction Control (DTC), and engine drag torque control (MSR).
  Riding Modes Pro adds the individually configurable “Race Pro” riding mode. Is the BMW F 450 RR suitable for the racetrack?
Yes. The supersport-specific geometry, low weight, 17-inch
  tires, “Race” riding mode, and reversible shift pattern are designed
  for sporty riding, including racetrack use. The Sport variant and both
  M Sport variants also feature the Sport suspension, whose 43 mm KYB
  upside-down fork offers adjustable rebound and compression damping.
  Riding Modes Pro additionally provides “Race Pro,” Sport screens, and
  a lap timer function. How suitable is the BMW F 450 RR for everyday use?
Despite its supersport focus, the BMW F 450 RR is equipped
  for everyday use. Standard features include a two-piece seat at a
  height of 790 mm, heated grips, LED lighting, a 6.5-inch TFT display,
  connectivity, and a USB-C port. With a WMTC fuel consumption of 3.8
  liters per 100 km, the 14-liter fuel tank provides a calculated range
  of more than 350 km. Accessories such as a tank bag and soft cases
  expand its versatility for commuting and short trips. Is the BMW F 450 RR also suitable for shorter riders, and what
    seat height does it offer?
Yes. The standard seat height of 790 mm (31.1 in) already
  provides excellent accessibility. Through the BMW Motorrad Original
  Accessories range, the riding position can be adjusted by raising the
  seat height by 20 mm (0.8 in) with the Sport Rider’s Seat or lowering
  it by 15 mm (0.6 in) with the Low Seat. This results in an available seat height range from 775 mm to 810 mm
  (30.5 in to 31.9 in), allowing riders, particularly those of shorter
  stature, to tailor the ergonomics to their individual needs. Which equipment variants are available?
The BMW F 450 RR is offered in four variants: Base, Sport,
  M Sport, and M Sport with Innovation Package. The Sport variant adds
  Shift Assistant Pro and the Sport suspension. M Sport additionally
  offers Riding Modes Pro and the Snaefell white / M Motorsport color
  scheme. The Innovation Package adds the Easy Ride Clutch. Munich, 13 May 2026. Watch the webcast of the public session of the 106th Annual General Meeting of BMW AG.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley - The Globe and Mail
content: Chicago, IL – October 15, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS, JPMorgan JPM and Morgan Stanley MS. The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. delivered impressive third-quarter 2026 results, driven by robust equities trading activity, higher investment banking (IB) fees, and growth in asset and wealth management revenues. The company's earnings per share jumped 39% year over year to $17.01, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 31.9%. Net revenues increased 23% to $18.68 billion, supported by a 72% surge in equities trading revenues and a 21% rise in investment banking fees. The company's annualized return on equity improved to 18.7% from 14.2% in the year-ago quarter, reflecting strong profitability. However, elevated operating expenses, relatively subdued fixed-income trading performance and uncertainties surrounding capital market activity remain concerning. Despite strong performance, the GS stock currently trades at a discount to the industry. The stock is trading at a forward price/earnings (P/E) of 12.53X, below the industry average of 12.60X. Its peers JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are trading at a P/E of 13.26X and 14.36X, respectively. Given these mixed factors, investors may wonder whether Goldman's solid earnings momentum makes the GS stock an attractive buy or whether a cautious approach is warranted. To answer this, let us delve deeper and analyze what will drive GS performance. Goldman continues to benefit from the recovery in global IB activity, supported by increased mergers and acquisitions (M&A), initial public offerings, and underwriting volumes. The momentum was also evident in the first nine months of 2026, with IB fees jumping 40% year over year to $9.46 billion. Advisory revenues rose 34% to $4.53 billion, while equity and debt underwriting revenues increased 73% and 29% to $2.19 billion and $2.75 billion, respectively. Looking ahead, Goldman's leadership position and robust deal pipeline bode well for continued growth. The company has maintained its #1 position in announced and completed M&A volumes and equity underwriting year to date, advising on $1.5 trillion of announced M&A transactions. Despite strong revenue generation in the third quarter, management indicated that its investment banking backlog remains robust, supported by sustained client engagement and replenishment in equity underwriting. Management continues to view the capital markets environment favorably, with opportunities arising from strategic dealmaking, technology investments and AI infrastructure financing. Although higher interest rates and macroeconomic uncertainties could affect deal activity, GS's leading market position and healthy pipeline position it well to capitalize on the ongoing investment banking recovery. Goldman continues to streamline its operations by exiting non-core consumer banking businesses and strengthening its core franchises. Under CEO David Solomon, the company has been strategically shifting its focus toward Global Banking & Markets (GBM) and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM), wherein it maintains strong competitive advantages and sees opportunities to build more durable revenue streams. In sync with these efforts, in August 2026, Goldman announced an agreement to acquire NEOS Investments, a provider of derivative income exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The acquisition is expected to increase Goldman's global active ETF assets under supervision to more than $90 billion, positioning it among the top eight providers by assets. The company also announced an agreement to acquire LCN Capital Partners, expanding its private real estate investment capabilities. In April 2026, Goldman acquired Innovator Capital Management, strengthening its active ETF offerings. In the same month, it completed the divestiture of its Polish asset management business, Goldman Sachs TFI, to ING Bank Slaski. These initiatives complement its broader efforts to reduce exposure to non-core consumer banking operations, including the transition of the General Motors credit card program in 2025 and the planned transfer of the Apple Card program to JPMorgan. The benefits of Goldman's strategic repositioning are increasingly evident in its financial performance. For the first nine months of 2026, GBM revenues jumped 34% to $41.72 billion, while AWM revenues rose 15% to $13.73 billion. Notably, management highlighted that durable revenues have more than doubled since its 2020 Investor Day and accounted for approximately 45% of the total revenues in the first nine months of 2026. These developments reflect Goldman's progress in building a more diversified earnings base, improving revenue stability and strengthening its long-term growth prospects. Goldman continues to accelerate its firmwide artificial intelligence transformation, focusing on improving productivity, streamlining operations and driving long-term operating leverage. The company is integrating AI across its core businesses, including trading, investment banking, asset management and internal operations, to enhance efficiency and strengthen its competitive position. In July 2026, Goldman's Asset Management unit launched AlphaAI, an AI-focused investment platform designed to capitalize on AI-driven investment opportunities across public and private markets. In May 2026, Goldman partnered with Anthropic, Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman to establish a $1.5-billion AI services venture designed to accelerate AI adoption across portfolio companies. These initiatives underscore the company's efforts to leverage AI for both investment opportunities and operational improvements. At the center of Goldman's transformation are One Goldman Sachs 3.0 (OneGS 3.0) and the GS AI Assistant program. OneGS 3.0 is a multi-year initiative focused on embedding AI into the company's operating model by simplifying workflows, automating processes, modernizing infrastructure and improving data management. Meanwhile, the GS AI Assistant is designed to enhance employee productivity by supporting information analysis, content generation and routine tasks, allowing professionals to focus on higher-value activities and client engagement. In the third-quarter 2026 earnings call, management highlighted significant opportunities arising from growing AI infrastructure investments, particularly increased demand for data centers and computing capacity. Goldman expects its financing, advisory and investment capabilities to position it favorably to capitalize on these opportunities. However, management also emphasized the need for disciplined underwriting and prudent risk management as AI-related financing requirements expand. Goldman's focus on operating efficiency is also reflected in its latest results. In the first nine months of 2026, the company's efficiency ratio improved to 59.4% from 62.1% in the year-ago period, reflecting better operating leverage and aligning with its 60% target. While investments in AI and technology may keep expenses elevated in the near term, continued automation and process improvements could enhance scalability, support revenue growth, and strengthen long-term profitability. Goldman maintains a strong balance sheet, supported by robust liquidity and capital levels. Its solid financial position allows the company to return capital to shareholders through share repurchases and regular dividend payments while maintaining sufficient flexibility to support business expansion. As of Sept. 30, 2026, Goldman's deposits totaled $568 billion, up from $558 billion as of June 30, 2026. Unsecured long-term borrowings stood at $352 billion. The company's average global core liquid assets increased to $574 billion in the third quarter from $555 billion in the preceding quarter, providing a substantial liquidity cushion. Meanwhile, its standardized Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 12.4%, 100 basis points above the current regulatory requirement of 11.4%. Following the Federal Reserve's 2026 stress test, GS increased its quarterly common stock dividend by 11% to $5 per share. Similarly, JPMorgan announced a 10% increase in its quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share in September. Morgan Stanley increased its quarterly dividend by 15% to $1.15 per share in the third quarter of 2026. In the third quarter of 2026, the company returned $4.49 billion to common shareholders, including $3 billion through share repurchases and $1.49 billion in dividends. In the first quarter of 2025, the board had approved a share repurchase program of up to $40 billion of common stock. As of Sept. 30, 2026, Goldman had nearly $19 billion worth of shares available under authorization.Supported by robust liquidity, solid earnings generation and capital levels above regulatory requirements, Goldman appears well-positioned to sustain shareholder-friendly capital distributions while pursuing growth opportunities. However, the pace of future buybacks will depend on regulatory capital requirements and business investment needs. Over the past seven days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings has remained unchanged. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Goldman's 2026 and 2027 earnings implies year-over-year growth of 31.5% and 6.9%, respectively. Shares of Goldman have jumped 16.1% in the past year, outperforming the industry's growth of 7.2%, and its peers JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley's rallies of 8.4% and 14.7%, respectively. Goldman's strong IB pipeline, solid trading performance and growing contribution from AWM revenues provide a favorable outlook for earnings growth. The company's strategic repositioning toward its core businesses, coupled with AI-driven efficiency initiatives, should support operating leverage and improve earnings stability over the long term. Further, its robust liquidity and capital position offer flexibility to pursue growth opportunities while maintaining shareholder-friendly capital distributions. However, sustaining the recent earnings momentum could prove challenging amid elevated operating expenses, relatively subdued fixed-income trading performance and uncertainties surrounding capital market activity. Moreover, although GS trades at a discount to the industry and its peers, the stock's 16.1% appreciation over the past year suggests that investors have already factored in some of its improving fundamentals. title: Big Banks Report Strong Earnings—So Why Are Shares Falling? - MarketBeat

It’s earnings season in the finance sector, and many banks are reporting earnings for the first time since the Federal Reserve's first interest rate hike since 2023. The hike was unanimous at 12-0, but the next move is anything but certain as we head into Q4. That uncertainty is weighing on banks as they report Q3 results this week, and on Oct. 13 we got results from Wells Fargo & Co. NYSE: WFC, The Goldman Sachs Group Inc. NYSE: GS, and Citigroup Inc. NYSE: C. Although the rate cut came too late to affect Q3 results, it still forces banks to update their outlooks, and their guidance and projections can offer investors clues. But despite the positive commentary, management projects $13 billion in NII for Q4 and left its full-year 2026 NII projection unchanged at $50 billion. The Q4 figure would represent 4% sequential growth, but Santomassimo noted that Markets NII is liability-sensitive, which could offset some fee growth in Q4. And while NII growth was strong, net interest margin was flat sequentially at 2.43%. Wells Fargo’s core revenue streams likely make it a winner in a high-rate environment, but the market didn’t respond well to management's “just trust me” guidance heading into Q4. The stock ended the day down 3%, but the price rejection at the 200-day moving average could have a longer impact. With the company saying rate benefits are basically punted into 2027, investors see a shaky road ahead for WFC shares, and the Relative Strength Index (RSI) staying under 50 suggests buyers are starting to thin out. But the dealmaking engine keeps churning, and this optimism likely helped the stock outperform peers who also reported on Oct. 13. CEO David Solomon noted that Q3 started with dealmaking activity at a five-year high and remains robust despite a late-quarter slowdown that pushed back several high-profile IPOs. The company has announced more than $1.5 trillion in M&A so far in 2026, which is more than $400 billion above the next closest competitor. Rate volatility could still impact dealmaking in future quarters, but today’s deal flow remains strong. GS shares started the day up nearly 5% before giving back all its gains at then some and closing down 0.17%. This is the best performance of the three, but it's notable given Goldman’s strong earnings relative to the two deposit banks. Despite the RSI hitting extremely oversold levels, the stock's decline below the 50-day and 200-day moving averages dampens short-term momentum, and the market needs more rate clarity before this trend can reverse. Citigroup raised NII projections while Wells Fargo left them flat. So why did Citigroup’s stock get punished more that day? The answer lies further in the guidance. Luchetti says the guidance could be conservative, but the market disliked the news, and the stock fell sharply during the day, closing down more than 5.5%. Despite the poor earnings reaction, C stock still has the most promising chart. title: Mending the fabric of your genes - HDBuzz
content: In plain language. Written by scientists.For the global HD community. Cells constantly mend tears and rips in the fabric of your DNA, like a cherished pair of jeans. Sometimes this mending can add C-A-Gs by mistake. A group of scientists examined whether other kinds of rips in the genetic fabric may be occurring in HD. Mending your genes is a bit like mending your jeans, with many different scuffs, rips, and loose threads in need of repair. Scientists know that a specific kind of DNA threading mistake causes the repeated C-A-Gs of HD to get longer and longer. But could other kinds of genetic mending also be involved in HD? A research group decided to assess a broad range of DNA repair activities in HD mice, to see what other kinds of genetic repairs might be happening. They showed that mending of double-stranded DNA breaks is increased in brains of HD mice and might contribute to  disease. The repeating genetic letters C-A-G are responsible for causing HD when someone inherits too many in a row in a gene called huntingtin. Over the past few years, major advances in HD research have shown that these problematic threads of repeating C-A-G can get longer and longer in some vulnerable neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information, through a process called somatic expansionsomatic expansion A process in which the CAG repeat in the Huntingtin gene can change over a person’s lifetime in some cells of the body, particularly in the brain.. By targeting somatic expansionsomatic expansion A process in which the CAG repeat in the Huntingtin gene can change over a person’s lifetime in some cells of the body, particularly in the brain., we might be able to preserve sick neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information and treat HD. However, scientists continue to debate how many repeated C-A-Gs cause a neuronneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information to get sick and lead to HD and whether all expansions are harmful. Your genetic code is packaged up as a double-strand of DNA in every cell of your body, like an extraordinary thread woven into genetic fabric. But as with any fabric, it can fray and develop holes over time. Fortunately, your body has many ways to spot damage to DNA and is equipped with a range of tools to repair it. Sometimes this damage is a partial break of only one DNA strand, called a single-strand break, like a frayed spot in your jeans where some threads remain. Other times the DNA double strand breaks completely, called a double-strand break, like a complete tear that leaves a hole. The DNA double strand can also be paired incorrectly, called a mismatch, like a thread that snags and pulls out. Your body is constantly mending these different kinds of DNA damage to keep the vital genetic fabric of your cells intact. In recent years, HD researchers have dug deeper on a surprising insight about how HD develops: those growing C-A-G repeats that can accumulate and eventually become toxic seem to happen as a byproduct of your body’s attempts to mend mismatched DNA. You read that right – C-A-G expansions can happen when the body is trying to repair slipped threads of DNA. While the mending is normally beneficial, repairing a C-A-G thread can sometimes actually add a few extra C-A-Gs by accident, like a tailor adding too much thread. It is increasingly thought that this is how so many C-A-Gs accumulate and become toxic in neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information – through errors made in repairing mismatched C-A-G threads. Although scientists have found that DNA mismatch repair can cause extra C-A-Gs to accumulate, it’s not clear whether other kinds of DNA mending might also be involved in HD. Understanding which kinds of DNA mending are disrupted in HD is important for developing the right kinds of drugs to treat all aspects of the disease. That’s where a new study comes in: Drs. Aris Polyzos and Cynthia McMurray from the Berkeley National Laboratory decided to look at what other kinds of DNA repair might be involved in HD. They asked whether double-strand breaks of DNA – clean cuts in the genetic fabric – are also a feature of the disease. Think of all the different kinds of tears and scuffs that your favorite pair of jeans might encounter. Mending each specific tear might require different stitching or technique. In the same way, your body has a suite of tailoring tools for all the different ways that your DNA fabric can fray and become damaged. Polyzos and colleagues looked at the brains of mice with HD to see how much these different kinds of DNA mending are happening. They found that the brains and neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information of HD mice have more mending associated with double stranded DNA breaks – a process distinct from mismatch repair. This raises an important question: does this mending of double-stranded DNA breaks happen in combination with accumulating C-A-Gs caused by mismatch repair, or does it happen independently? And might these double-stranded breaks be involved in HD? To try to answer this tricky question, the researchers looked at double-stranded DNA breaks in HD mice that have a lot of C-A-Gs but are engineered so that their cells are missing some of the machinery involved in mismatch repair. These mice engineered without mismatch repair don’t accumulate more C-A-Gs, since mismatch repair mistakes are how more C-A-Gs get added. Interestingly, in both the HD mice that accumulate more C-A-Gs and the mice that don’t, there were still more double-stranded DNA breaks than in healthy mice. These findings suggest that double-stranded breaks in the DNA fabric might be happening independently of mismatch repair and accumulating C-A-Gs. In these experiments, the authors showed that different types of DNA damage – double strand breaks and mismatch repair – can happen independently of one another in HD mice. This means that preventing extra double-stranded breaks in DNA of the brain might also be important for treating HD. There are still important questions about how these findings apply to people with HD. The researchers studied mice with far more CAG repeats than most people with HD inherit. At these very long repeat lengths, mice can develop disease-related changes even without further CAG expansion. This makes it difficult to establish whether DNA double-strand breaks contribute to HD in the same way in people, where CAG repeats typically start much shorter and can expand in some cells over many years. Further studies will be needed to determine whether these DNA breaks are a direct cause of neuronal damage in human HD, or one part of a more complex chain of events. Nonetheless, this research continues to expand our understanding of what goes wrong in neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information of people with HD – and how to mend it. Goldman Sachs' baseline forecast projects a December rate hike by the Federal Reserve, with rate cuts beginning in September 2027. If long-term interest rates remain elevated, the drag on GDP in 2027 could exceed 0.4 percentage points, with core inflation and long-term interest rates serving as key variables. According to Woofun AI, Goldman Sachs (GS.US)'s macro research briefing has established a baseline scenario for the Federal Reserve's policy trajectory: it expects the final rate hike in December, followed by the start of a rate-cutting cycle from September 2027, with three rate cuts. This timeline directly points to the long-term suppressive effects of a high-interest-rate environment on the real economy, rather than merely a short-term policy shift. The structural stickiness of inflation data underpins the current policy impasse at the micro level. According to the U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) data for September, released on October 14, overall inflation rose 0.6% month-over-month, while the year-on-year increase remained steady at 3.7%. A closer analysis of this rise reveals that the energy sector accounted for more than half of the monthly increase, with gasoline prices surging 9.1% month-over-month—this sharp jump was the primary driver behind the expansion of the headline CPI from 0.4% in August to 0.6%. However, attributing inflation solely to energy price volatility would be overly simplistic. Excluding food and energy, the core CPI rose 0.3% month-over-month, unchanged from August, indicating that underlying price pressures have not eased substantially. Even more noteworthy is the trend in housing prices, which posted a month-over-month increase of 0.4%, up from 0.3% in August. The persistent behavior of this core indicator makes it difficult for the market to explain the full picture of current inflation solely in terms of fluctuations in energy prices. For the Federal Reserve, the key variable lies in the persistence of price increases: while energy prices can quickly push up headline inflation, their longer‑term effects depend on how cost pass‑through mechanisms operate; meanwhile, whether core inflation can decelerate steadily will directly shape policymakers' assessment of underlying price pressures. At present, the available data are insufficient to confirm that inflation has entered a sustained downward trajectory, and the lack of further evidence of cooling in core inflation provides logical support for maintaining a tight monetary policy stance. Woofun AI's analysis shows that Goldman Sachs' (GS.US) estimates of the cost of growth are highly sensitive to assumptions about the interest-rate path. Under the baseline scenario—where the Federal Reserve raises rates once in December, long-term rates decline from current levels over the next few months, and rate cuts begin in late 2027—Goldman Sachs (GS.US) estimates that higher interest rates will weigh on U.S. GDP growth by approximately 0.2 percentage points in 2027. This figure is neither a forecast of U.S. GDP growth nor an indication that the economy will contract by 0.2 percent; rather, it represents the model's estimate of the marginal loss in growth. However, if interest rates remain at their current levels and do not decline, this drag could more than double the baseline projection—exceeding 0.4 percentage points. The substantial gap between these two scenarios underscores the report's central conclusion: future growth pressures will hinge not only on the Federal Reserve's short-term policy rate but also on whether market‑based financing costs fall in tandem. While the Fed directly influences short-term funding rates, the cost of housing loans, long-term corporate financing, and investment projects is heavily shaped by longer‑term market rates. Consequently, even if the Fed halts its tightening cycle, persistently high long-term rates would prevent businesses and households from immediately benefiting from lower borrowing costs, leaving housing demand, business investment, and credit activity under continued strain. Compared with the impact of a single rate hike, the sustained burden of elevated financing costs could generate far greater cumulative adverse effects. The ultimate trajectory of policy depends on whether the dual conditions of moderating core inflation and declining long-term interest rates are met. Goldman Sachs (GS.US) bases its projected timing for rate cuts on the premise that core inflation will show more sustained moderation; if price increases remain stubbornly high or energy costs continue to spill over into other goods and services, the period of monetary tightening could be extended, and expectations for rate cuts would likely be reassessed. Meanwhile, the decline of long-term interest rates from their current levels is a key assumption underlying Goldman Sachs' (GS.US) more moderate growth forecast. If long-term rates remain elevated, even if policy rates no longer rise consecutively, financing costs could continue to weigh on demand. From an asset pricing perspective, investors must distinguish between a policy shift and an improvement in the financing environment: halting rate hikes may ease concerns about further tightening, but whether growth pressures ease will depend on whether real borrowing costs actually fall. The key variables to watch going forward are clearly defined: whether core inflation decelerates persistently, whether long-term rates retreat, and whether housing, investment, and employment begin to show more pronounced signs of strain. If inflationary stickiness forces financing costs to stay high for a longer period, the cost to the U.S. economy will be significantly higher than the 0.2 percentage points projected in Goldman Sachs' (GS.US) baseline scenario. title: PTSC Marine GS, Pacifico Energy launch surveys for 1.8 GW offshore wind projects - Theinvestor
content:
Pacifico Energy Vietnam Co. and Vietnam Petroleum Technical Services Corporation (PTSC), through its PTSC Marine GS branch, on Tuesday launched survey work for two offshore wind power projects in Vietnam. Pacifico Energy Vietnam Co. is a member of U.S.-based Pacifico Energy Group, while PTSC is a subsidiary of state-owned Petrovietnam. The event marks a key step in Pacifico Energy's renewable energy development plans in Vietnam, moving from legal and regulatory procedures to actual offshore technical surveys. The launch ceremony was held at PTSC Marine GS headquarters in Rach Dua ward, Ho Chi Minh City. Pacifico Energy was represented by Pham Quoc Anh, executive chairman of Pacifico Energy Vietnam; Dhiraj Shangari, director of capital markets and investments at PE Group; and Nguyen Quynh Giang, general director of Pacifico Energy Vietnam. PTSC representatives included Le Chien Thang, deputy general director of the corporation, and Trinh Huu Duong, director of PTSC Marine GS, as well as executives from PTSC and PTSC Marine GS. In 2026, Pacifico Energy received approval from Vietnam's Ministry of Agriculture and Environment to use designated marine areas for surveys supporting two major offshore wind projects. The Southern offshore wind project has planned capacity of 500 MW, located in waters off Ho Chi Minh City. The South Central offshore wind project No. 3, located in waters off Lam Dong province, has planned capacity of 1,300 MW. With a combined planned capacity of 1.8 GW, the projects could attract more than $6 billion in investment in subsequent development phases, positioning Pacifico Energy among the foreign investors at the forefront of Vietnam's offshore wind sector. The survey campaign will begin with geophysical and meteorological-oceanographic surveys to collect data on seabed topography, geological characteristics and natural conditions. These studies are a crucial foundation for technical assessments, engineering design, and the overall development plans for the projects. Pacifico Energy's selection of PTSC, one of Vietnam's leading offshore engineering service providers, to undertake the initial survey package reflects a combination of international experience and domestic technical expertise and offshore infrastructure. The partnership also offers opportunities for Vietnamese companies to participate more deeply in the offshore wind supply chain, spanning surveys, port logistics, mechanical fabrication, construction and operations. Speaking at the event, Pham Quoc Anh, executive chairman of Pacifico Energy Vietnam, said the launch of the technical survey campaign reaffirmed the group's long-term commitment to Vietnam. "We believe offshore wind can provide large-scale clean electricity while helping establish a new industry, create jobs and open up opportunities for Vietnamese businesses. Our partnership with PTSC is a concrete step towards realizing that vision," he said. Le Chien Thang, PTSC's deputy general director, said the corporation continued to strengthen its competitiveness by drawing on years of experience in offshore projects and upgrading its capabilities to meet the stringent standards of the renewable energy supply chain. The contract further affirmed PTSC's leading position in renewable energy services in Vietnam and the wider region, he said. Arati Shroff, acting U.S. consul general in Ho Chi Minh City, praised the cooperation between the two companies, describing it as a practical example of efforts to advance clean energy initiatives and contribute to the Vietnam-U.S. Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The survey launch came shortly after a September 23, 2026 meeting in New York between Vietnam's Party General Secretary and President To Lam and Nate Franklin, chairman and founder of Pacifico Energy Group. The rapid commencement of offshore technical activities underscores the group's determination to translate its investment commitments into concrete action. title: Should You Buy, Hold or Sell Goldman Stock Post Impressive Q3 Results? - TradingView
content: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS delivered impressive third-quarter 2026 results, driven by robust equities trading activity, higher investment banking (IB) fees, and growth in asset and wealth management revenues. The company's earnings per share jumped 39% year over year to $17.01, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 31.9%. Net revenues increased 23% to $18.68 billion, supported by a 72% surge in equities trading revenues and a 21% rise in investment banking fees. The company's annualized return on equity improved to 18.7% from 14.2% in the year-ago quarter, reflecting strong profitability. However, elevated operating expenses, relatively subdued fixed-income trading performance and uncertainties surrounding capital market activity remain concerning. Despite strong performance, the GS stock currently trades at a discount to the industry. The stock is trading at a forward price/earnings (P/E) of 12.53X, below the industry average of 12.60X. Its peers JPMorgan JPM and Morgan Stanley MS are trading at a P/E of 13.26X and 14.36X, respectively. Given these mixed factors, investors may wonder whether Goldman's solid earnings momentum makes the GS stock an attractive buy or whether a cautious approach is warranted. To answer this, let us delve deeper and analyze what will drive GS performance. Goldman continues to benefit from the recovery in global IB activity, supported by increased mergers and acquisitions (M&A), initial public offerings, and underwriting volumes. The momentum was also evident in the first nine months of 2026, with IB fees jumping 40% year over year to $9.46 billion. Advisory revenues rose 34% to $4.53 billion, while equity and debt underwriting revenues increased 73% and 29% to $2.19 billion and $2.75 billion, respectively. Looking ahead, Goldman's leadership position and robust deal pipeline bode well for continued growth. The company has maintained its #1 position in announced and completed M&A volumes and equity underwriting year to date, advising on $1.5 trillion of announced M&A transactions. Despite strong revenue generation in the third quarter, management indicated that its investment banking backlog remains robust, supported by sustained client engagement and replenishment in equity underwriting. Management continues to view the capital markets environment favorably, with opportunities arising from strategic dealmaking, technology investments and AI infrastructure financing. Although higher interest rates and macroeconomic uncertainties could affect deal activity, GS's leading market position and healthy pipeline position it well to capitalize on the ongoing investment banking recovery. Goldman continues to streamline its operations by exiting non-core consumer banking businesses and strengthening its core franchises. Under CEO David Solomon, the company has been strategically shifting its focus toward Global Banking & Markets (GBM) and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM), wherein it maintains strong competitive advantages and sees opportunities to build more durable revenue streams. In sync with these efforts, in August 2026, Goldman announced an agreement to acquire NEOS Investments, a provider of derivative income exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The acquisition is expected to increase Goldman's global active ETF assets under supervision to more than $90 billion, positioning it among the top eight providers by assets. The company also announced an agreement to acquire LCN Capital Partners, expanding its private real estate investment capabilities. In April 2026, Goldman acquired Innovator Capital Management, strengthening its active ETF offerings. In the same month, it completed the divestiture of its Polish asset management business, Goldman Sachs TFI, to ING Bank Slaski. These initiatives complement its broader efforts to reduce exposure to non-core consumer banking operations, including the transition of the General Motors credit card program in 2025 and the planned transfer of the Apple Card program to JPMorgan. The benefits of Goldman's strategic repositioning are increasingly evident in its financial performance. For the first nine months of 2026, GBM revenues jumped 34% to $41.72 billion, while AWM revenues rose 15% to $13.73 billion. Notably, management highlighted that durable revenues have more than doubled since its 2020 Investor Day and accounted for approximately 45% of the total revenues in the first nine months of 2026. These developments reflect Goldman's progress in building a more diversified earnings base, improving revenue stability and strengthening its long-term growth prospects. Goldman continues to accelerate its firmwide artificial intelligence transformation, focusing on improving productivity, streamlining operations and driving long-term operating leverage. The company is integrating AI across its core businesses, including trading, investment banking, asset management and internal operations, to enhance efficiency and strengthen its competitive position. In July 2026, Goldman's Asset Management unit launched AlphaAI, an AI-focused investment platform designed to capitalize on AI-driven investment opportunities across public and private markets. In May 2026, Goldman partnered with Anthropic, Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman to establish a $1.5-billion AI services venture designed to accelerate AI adoption across portfolio companies. These initiatives underscore the company's efforts to leverage AI for both investment opportunities and operational improvements. At the center of Goldman's transformation are One Goldman Sachs 3.0 (OneGS 3.0) and the GS AI Assistant program. OneGS 3.0 is a multi-year initiative focused on embedding AI into the company's operating model by simplifying workflows, automating processes, modernizing infrastructure and improving data management. Meanwhile, the GS AI Assistant is designed to enhance employee productivity by supporting information analysis, content generation and routine tasks, allowing professionals to focus on higher-value activities and client engagement. In the third-quarter 2026 earnings call, management highlighted significant opportunities arising from growing AI infrastructure investments, particularly increased demand for data centers and computing capacity. Goldman expects its financing, advisory and investment capabilities to position it favorably to capitalize on these opportunities. However, management also emphasized the need for disciplined underwriting and prudent risk management as AI-related financing requirements expand. Goldman's focus on operating efficiency is also reflected in its latest results. title: LG Electronics Partners with GS Engineering & Construction, GRC on Immersion Cooling for AI Data Centers - 조선일보
content: Collaboration integrates cooling tech, architectural designs, and system performance for real-world data center solutions LG Electronics has partnered with GS Engineering & Construction and U.S.-based immersion cooling specialist GRC to jointly develop immersion cooling technology and standard designs for AI data centers. The collaboration aims to validate not only the performance of cooling equipment but also building structures, piping, power connections, and other elements to create an integrated solution applicable to real-world data centers. LG Electronics announced on October 14 that it signed a business agreement with the two companies on October 13 at GS Engineering & Construction’s headquarters in Jongno-gu, Seoul, to advance immersion cooling technology and facility solutions for data centers. Attendees included Oh Se-gi, vice president and head of the ES Research Institute at LG Electronics; Jo Seong-han, vice president and head of the Future Technology Division at GS Engineering & Construction; and Choi Dong-hoon, director and head of GRC’s Korean branch. Immersion cooling is a technology that submerges electronic components like GPUs and CPUs in electrically non-conductive cooling oil to dissipate heat. Unlike cold plate methods, where coolant flows through internal channels attached to chips, the cooling oil directly contacts components to absorb heat. The heated oil is then cooled via a heat exchanger and recirculated, reducing the need for server fans. Practical implementation requires considerations such as tank placement, structural load, piping, power connections, and maintenance space. In this collaboration, LG Electronics will provide air cooling, liquid cooling, and immersion cooling technologies alongside operational data, and build cooling solutions based on the jointly developed standard design. GS Engineering & Construction will establish standard architectural designs for data centers and operate a testbed for pre-verification, demonstrating equipment layout, structural load, piping, and power connections. GRC will supply immersion tanks and control technologies, contributing to system performance improvements based on installation, operation, and maintenance data. LG Electronics previously reviewed the feasibility of immersion cooling technology and commercialization with SK Enmove and GRC. Last month, it also signed an agreement with SK Enmove to jointly develop coolant, chiller oil, and immersion cooling technologies. By integrating construction companies’ architectural and facility design capabilities into its existing collaboration—focused on validating coolant-equipment combinations—the company aims to enhance on-site applicability. LG Electronics possesses technologies for chillers that produce cold water, fan wall units that supply cool air and exhaust heat, cooling water distribution units (CDUs), and cold plates. It plans to verify the performance and reliability of immersion cooling technology, supply cooling solutions tailored to data centers’ heat output and design conditions, and expand related business operations.

(GFUZ) made history on Monday, becoming the first pure-play nuclear fusion energy company to trade on a major public stock exchange. In an exclusive interview with Stocktwits, CEO Greg Twinney argued that fusion is not just a cleaner alternative to fission but is a fundamentally larger market opportunity. GFUZ stock surged 21% on its debut, added over 25% on Tuesday, and was trading about 2.5% lower in the overnight session. The Vancouver-based company, backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, among others, went public through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III, which provided General Fusion with approximately $150 million in cash. Earlier, Twinney told the Wall Street Journal that the funding is sufficient to meet the scientific milestones required by its demonstration machine. The listing arrives at a pivotal moment. Surging electricity demand driven by the AI boom, the global spread of electrification, and the energy appetite of large-scale computing has renewed urgency around new sources of firm, clean power. Fusion has attracted growing investment and government attention as a potential long-term answer. According to the Financial Times, the number of private fusion companies has more than doubled over the past five years, intensifying competition at a time when the technology is still roughly a decade from commercialization. General Fusion is targeting its first commercial plant around 2035. Twinney's bull case for fusion starts with what it doesn't produce. Unlike fission, fusion does not generate long-lived radioactive waste, does not use fuels that could be weaponized, and carries no risk of a meltdown. "Fusion is just inherently safe. We're not needing to engineer safety into it in the same way that you need to with fission," he told Stocktwits. "When fusion fails, it kind of just fails safely and there's not really any fallout from that." That safety profile has a direct commercial implication: regulators around the world are moving to govern fusion "in a much lighter way" than conventional nuclear, Twinney said, which he believes creates the potential to site fusion plants closer to population centers and industrial demand. That's a significant advantage over fission, which requires remote, heavily secured facilities. "We get all the benefits that fission can provide without the downsides," he said. There's another significant advantage. Fusion reactors primarily use deuterium, which can be extracted from seawater and is "massively abundant." The other component, tritium, is rarer in nature but can be bred through the interaction of a neutron and lithium. Fission, by contrast, relies on uranium and other finite sources. "The overall market size because of the safety profile and the abundance of fuel in fusion is much bigger than fission," Twinney said. While advanced nuclear companies such as Oklo Inc. (OKLO) and NuScale Power Corp. (SMR) are often thought of as being closer to commercialization than fusion technology, Twinney said that the gap may not be as large as investors assume. While the road to commercialization for fusion technology has its challenges, including achieving reactor durability, tritium fuel breeding, economic viability, and the ability to efficiently extract and convert fusion energy into electricity, he argues small modular reactor (SMR) timelines also struggle with regulatory hurdles that can make timelines less predictable than they appear today. "I know that the timelines for SMRs, which can be very unpredictable due to regulations and those types of things, [are] probably not that different," he said. According to Twinney, the combination of abundant fuel supplies and a lighter regulatory framework could ultimately enable fusion to scale faster than conventional nuclear technologies once commercial viability has been demonstrated. However, Twinney does not view fusion and fission as mutually exclusive technologies. "They will be complementing each other," he said. "And I think that fusion kind of rounds out the nuclear circle if you think about it that way," he added. When asked about criticism from former Commonwealth Fusion Systems CTO Dan Brunner, who, in a recent interview with the Financial Times, said General Fusion's commercialization timeline was "very hard to believe," Twinney said the company’s timelines were based on real experimental results from its Lawson Machine 26. The machine is designed to demonstrate that plasma can be heated through mechanical compression rather than superconducting magnets or high-powered lasers, he said, adding that the company's early results validated the operating principles behind its MTF approach that are “not based on fiction or papers being written.” The timelines “are based on our real results from machines that we have built and operated and then eventually written papers on. But those are real results papers, not theoretical papers,” he said. Twinney also emphasized that General Fusion's approach could offer a cost advantage over many competing technologies. While many other fusion developers rely on expensive superconducting magnets, high-powered lasers, or advanced materials that have yet to be proven at commercial scale, General Fusion's Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF) system uses mechanical compression and a liquid-lithium wall that can protect reactor components from neutron damage, help with breeding tritium fuel, and absorbing fusion energy as heat that can be converted into electricity using conventional steam turbines. In an earlier interview with Stocktwits, Chief Strategy Officer Megan Wilson had also pointed to the economic advantages of MTF, which eliminate the need for expensive magnets, targets, lasers, or exotic, not-yet-invented materials. The technology also eliminates the need for frequent replacement of components damaged by neutron exposure, she had said. “Our plants are designed to be cost-competitive compared to coal, steam, and natural gas,” she had said then. “They are expected to deliver four times as much energy per unit of fuel as fission, without long-lived radioactive waste, positioning them as the superior nuclear technology for sustainable growth.” By avoiding costly magnets and lasers and using existing industrial technologies, Twinney said he believes General Fusion has a clearer path to building an economically viable power plant, as the company’s design has from the beginning aimed to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. "What we are trying to do at General Fusion, and our power plant design from the beginning, has been we want to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. Not just demonstrate a bunch of fusion, but actually avoid the barriers to commercializing it," he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GFUZ stock is ‘bullish’ amid ‘high’ message volumes.
