The Goldman Sachs Group Inc (NYSE:GS) reported net revenues of $18.7 billion, the second highest in its history, with EPS of $17.01 and an ROE of 18.7%. Investment banking advisory revenues reached a record, maintaining the number one position in M&A with a backlog that remains very robust. Equities net revenues were $6.4 billion, up 72% year over year, driven by strong performance in both intermediation and financing. Asset and Wealth Management revenues grew 14% year over year to $5.1 billion, with record management fees and assets under supervision of $4.1 trillion. The Goldman Sachs Group Inc (NYSE:GS) has built a higher and more durable revenue base, with durable revenues now representing approximately 45% of year-to-date revenues. The Goldman Sachs Group Inc (NYSE:GS) faces ongoing geopolitical tensions and energy supply disruptions that add complexity to the economic outlook. Rising oil prices and inflation concerns have led to higher bond yields and expectations of further rate hikes, which could impact market activity. Provision for credit losses was $368 million, reflecting certain impairments and overall growth in lending, indicating potential credit quality concerns. Non-compensation expenses increased 30% year over year, driven largely by higher transaction-based expenses, pressuring overall expenses. The Goldman Sachs Group Inc (NYSE:GS) acknowledges uncertainty in the AI investment cycle, with risks of overcapacity and potential financing constraints that could affect future returns. Q: Glenn Schorr of Evercore asked whether there was anything unique in the quarter that shouldn't be over-modeled into Q4, and how Goldman is positioning its markets business against structural developments like tokenization, agentic trading, DeFi vaults and prediction markets.A: CEO David Solomon said there was nothing unusual to call out in the quarter. On market structure, he noted Goldman has repeatedly adapted to technological change, citing electronification of equities as a precedent where the opportunity set ultimately expanded. He said tokenization is an important trend across asset classes, that Goldman supported the CLARITY Act for the market clarity it would provide, and that the firm is engaged with agencies providing rules in the absence of legislation. Goldman has invested in digital asset market infrastructure for years, built its own digital asset rails (GSDAP), tokenized bonds and money market funds, and participated in the July launch of DTCC's tokenization service. He stressed current activity is very small and at the margin, but that the technology could drive efficiency, automation, lower costs and better liquidity over time. Q: Glenn Schorr and later Mike Mayo asked David Solomon directly about press reports of an accelerated succession process and his plans as CEO.A: Solomon said the articles "create noise" and stated plainly: "There is no succession transition or timeline underway at Goldman Sachs." He said he is pleased with the firm's progress since Investor Day, is "really enjoying the job," and that he and the Board are singularly focused on growing the firm, growing earnings and serving clients. Q: Erika Najarian of UBS asked whether the global bond rout and higher long-end rates are chilling activity, and how to think about capital consumption in Q4 given the lighter capital ratio and expectations of an active trading quarter.A: Solomon said the firm runs a 50-to-100 basis point capital buffer, generates capital through good earnings momentum, and feels comfortable deploying into an active fourth quarter while remaining nimble allocating to clients first and returning excess to shareholders. On rates, he noted roughly a 75 basis point move in the 10-year since early July, but argued a 5% 10-year Treasury is not alarming by historical standards; abrupt moves, not absolute levels, create market headwinds. He characterized the current environment as "top quartile" for capital markets activity versus a "top decile" environment in late May/June, supported by a resilient economy, a tech supercycle and a pro-strategic-activity regulatory backdrop. Q: Ebrahim Poonawala of Bank of America asked whether financing will be the real choke point for AI capex given higher rates and unclear returns, and separately how equities financing growth makes earnings more durable rather than more cyclical.A: Solomon said "I don't know and nobody knows" on the AI financing trajectory, but acknowledged the scale of projected data center investment carries risks, including crowding out and pressure on rates that could affect project returns. He said Goldman sits at the center of the ecosystem but is highly disciplined about what it underwrites, and that demand for compute currently far exceeds supply. On prime and equities financing, he said there will be cyclicality when equity markets fall and leverage unwinds, but over three-to-five-year periods the business is fundamentally correlated to global GDP and market cap growth. He noted firmwide revenues compounded 11% since 2022, which he does not expect to repeat, but said the durable base is much larger and more diverse. title: 44-year-old Bay Area pizza spot taking over shuttered Bobby G’s location - Berkeleyside
content:

Add Berkeleyside as a Preferred Source on Google so you never miss our reporting when you search.🔍 North Beach Pizza’s Berkeley branch is moving from one side of downtown to the other. Gustavo Ramirez, who helps run the restaurant and is the son of North Beach Pizza Berkeley’s owner of the same name, confirmed to Nosh that the pizza spot will be relocating to 2072 University Ave. (near the corner of Shattuck Avenue), which formerly housed Bobby G’s Pizzeria. The San Francisco pizza chain was first opened in the North Beach neighborhood in 1982 by Brazilian native and Bay Area businessman Altamir Souza, whose price-friendly menu and early adoption of a digital delivery system appealed to San Franciscans looking for a quick bite. Four years later, Souza opened his second location a block away, before moving on to open three others across the city. Souza later expanded across the Bay to San Mateo, Daly City, Half Moon Bay and Berkeley. Over the last few decades, the restaurant chain has switched ownership across its locations. Now, Ramirez’s family owns seven of the remaining restaurants, while Souza owns the remaining one in San Francisco’s Outer Sunset neighborhood. According to Ramirez, this isn’t just a relocation — it’s a homecoming. “So years ago we were actually located on University Avenue at 1598 University Ave. and North Beach Pizza was there for many years,” Ramirez explained. “But then the land was sold to developers so we had to move and we relocated to where we are now, 2420 Shattuck Ave.” Bobby G’s abruptly closed in April, following a lawsuit from a former employee and, as Nosh reported, a pattern of delayed payments and other managerial issues. Once the former Bobby G’s space became available, Ramirez and his family jumped at the chance to sign a lease. “It was just really ideal, really perfect. Everything kind of lined up perfectly for us to be able to make that move back to University Avenue,” Ramirez said. “We signed a lease this month in Berkeley, and we’ve been fixing things up and getting the store ready. And if all goes well, we expect to open within the next few weeks.” Ramirez also confirmed that the restaurant’s menu won’t change, and patrons can expect classics like the pepperoni pizza, cheese stromboli, and crispy chicken parmigiana, alongside its more unique offerings, like the Alcatraz pizza, a ranch sauced pizza pie topped with chicken, gorgonzola, red onions and a spiral of Buffalo sauce. Off-schedule CEO commentary of this kind from a major investment bank is typically delivered at a conference or around a results window, and it has historically functioned as a soft trading update: a directional read on the advisory and underwriting pipeline rather than a quantified one. The useful distinction is between the two engines being referenced, M&A advisory and capital markets issuance, since a constructive tone can reflect a large signed-but-unannounced advisory backlog, strong ECM and DCM calendars, or both, and past episodes have shown these do not always move together. Such remarks from this house also carry read-across to the peer set, as the large US investment banks tend to describe the same fee environment within days of each other, and their commentary has on previous occasions clustered ahead of visibly better or worse industry fee prints. The tell is whether peers echo the characterization and whether any supporting datapoint follows, such as backlog language or announced mandates, since a CEO tone without corroboration has historically faded quickly from the tape. Equities in the sector have tended to treat this as confirmation of an existing trend rather than new information, with the larger moves reserved for the formal revenue disclosure. title: CVS Ferrari expands German dealer network with GS-Gabelstapler service - American Journal of Transportation
content:
AJOT Newsroom
	

		 | Oct 13 2026 at 09:44 AM  | Logistics CVS Ferrari is expanding its sales and customer support network in Germany through a new partnership with GS- Gabelstapler Service GmbH. GS-Gabelstapler Service GmbH is the first independent dealer appointed by CVS Ferrari Deutschland in the German-speaking market of Germany, Austria and Switzerland. CVS Ferrari plans to add more regional partners over time. GS-Gabelstapler Service supports the movement, storage, and handling of materials within warehouses, terminals, and industrial facilities. Its services include new and used forklift sales, parts, maintenance, rentals, operator training, and equipment financing, including leasing and installment-purchase options. GS will also add CVS heavy-duty lift trucks to its rental and demonstration fleet. CVS Director, Robert Taylor, said, “CVS is so proud to bring GS Gabelstapler into our growing family in Europe. It is an honor for such an astute material handling company to be representing our product. We look for a great future together, serving our customers.” Kai-Norman Knötsch, Managing Director of CVS Ferrari Deutschland, commented, “Our customers expect advice and service to be available as close to them as possible. With GS, we have found a partner who knows its region and its requirements extremely well. For us, this marks the beginning of a network that we intend to expand step by step in order to provide even better support to our customers.” Torsten Franke, Managing Director of GS-Gabelstapler Service, remarked, “We have known our customers’ requirements for decades and know where heavy-duty equipment is needed. With CVS, we are expanding our product range and closing a gap in our portfolio. Objective, partnership-based advice, comprehensive solutions and service have been the hallmarks of our company for more than 45 years. We are now delighted to be able to offer our customers CVS products for heavy-duty handling and container loading as well.” CVS Ferrari Deutschland supplies equipment for ports, terminals, industrial operations and other demanding material-handling applications. The product line includes reach stackers for loaded and empty containers, mast-style empty container handlers for depots and port facilities, high-capacity lift trucks, and terminal tractors available in two-wheel-drive and four-wheel-drive configurations. CVS reach stackers can stack containers up to six high. Certain mast-style empty container handlers can stack up to eight containers high and, depending on configuration, handle two empty containers at the same time. Heavy-duty lift trucks are available with rated capacities from 16 to 52 metric tons, approximately 35,300 to 114,600 pounds. Electric-drive empty container handlers and terminal tractors are also available to help customers address emissions and noise requirements at ports and terminals. “High-quality products, sound advice, and first-class service are what distinguish us. With GS, we now have a partner at our side who enables us to fully meet these requirements. For us, this marks the beginning of a network that we intend to expand step by step in order to provide even better support to our customers,” said Oliver Hoffmann, Sales Manager, CVS Ferrari Deutschland. content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results Goldman Sachs delivered record year-to-date revenues and robust Q3 results, with net revenues of $18.7B (second highest ever), EPS of $17.01, and ROE of 18.7%. Good morning. My name is [Katie] and I will be your conference facilitator today. I would like to welcome everyone to The Goldman Sachs third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. On behalf of Goldman Sachs, I will begin the call with the following disclaimer. The earnings presentation can be found on the investor relations page of the goldmansachs.com website and contains information on forward-looking statements and non-GAAP measures. This audiocast is copyrighted material of The Goldman Sachs Group Inc., and may not be duplicated, reproduced, or rebroadcast without consent. This call is being recorded today, October 13, 2026. I will now turn the call over to Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, David Solomon, and Chief Financial Officer, Denis Coleman. Thank you. Mr. Solomon, you may begin your conference. Thank you, operator. Good morning, everybody. Thank you for joining us. We delivered very strong performance in the third quarter, generating net revenues of $18.7 billion, the second highest in our history, earnings per share of $17.01, an ROE of 18.7%, and an ROTE of 20.5%. Our quarterly results included the impact of an accelerated charitable contribution. Excluding that contribution, quarterly EPS would've been approximately $18, and ROE and ROTE would've been approximately 20% and 21.5% respectively. For the year-to-date, we delivered record revenues driving an ROE of 20.7% and an ROTE of 22.4%. While the third quarter began with optimism around a potential resolution of the conflict in the Middle East, renewed geopolitical tensions and continued disruption of energy flows added complexity to the outlook, increasing oil prices, reigniting inflation concerns, and driving bond yields higher. Against this backdrop, the Fed raised rates in September for the first time in three years, with markets pricing in approximately 75 basis points of additional tightening in this cycle across the U.S., U.K., and Europe. Despite these crosscurrents, the health of the underlying U.S. economy has remained solid, with strong corporate earnings growth, GDP growth of 2.2%, and a very resilient labor market. In complex environments such as these, clients rely on the advice, execution, and intermediation expertise of Goldman Sachs to navigate uncertainty and advance their most important strategic priorities. In global banking and markets, we generated the second highest revenues in our history. Within investment banking, advisory revenues were a record, and we maintained our longstanding number one position in M&A, advising on $1.5 trillion of announced transactions for the year. We maintained our year-to-date lead over our closest peer of approximately $430 billion, the largest lead we've ever had, as clients turn to us for advice on significant transactions, including Hugging Face's $13 billion sale to NVIDIA and Integer Holdings' $6 billion sale to KKR. As you'll remember, we entered the quarter with our highest backlog in five years, and even with exceptionally strong revenue production in the quarter, our backlog remains very robust, reflecting the strength and breadth of client engagement across our leading investment banking franchise. In equities, we delivered our second-best performance after last quarter's record results, with strength across both intermediation and financing. In FICC, we remain steadfast in supporting our clients' global risk intermediation needs across asset classes amid sharp moves in rates and increased volatility in commodities. Importantly, financing activities have become a larger and more durable component of our markets businesses, representing over 40% of FICC and equities revenues year-to-date. This progress reflects strong client demand, prudent balance sheet deployment, and continued execution against our strategic priorities, including deliberate multi-year investments in Asia, which we highlighted earlier this year as an opportunity to drive further share gains. This dynamic market backdrop has also reinforced the importance of trusted advice and diversified investment solutions for asset and wealth management clients. Our scaled and durable platform brings together leading investment capabilities across public and private markets and delivers them through deep institutional relationships, our ultra-premier high net worth wealth management franchise, and our expanding third-party distribution network. The strength of this platform continues to drive exceptional growth at scale. In the third quarter, management and other fees increased 22% year-over-year to a record $3.6 billion and surpassed $10 billion for the year-to-date. Our assets under supervision reached another record of $4.1 trillion, supported by $97 billion of long-term net inflows, representing our 35th consecutive quarter of inflows. In wealth management, $47 billion of long-term net inflows contributed to record client assets of $2.1 trillion. For 2026, wealth management long-term net inflows are annualizing at 12%, well ahead of our 5% target, which underscores the strength of our client relationships built on trust and long-term performance. In alternatives, we are driving strong growth, with alternative assets under supervision up 26% year-over-year to a record $491 billion. We continue to see strong momentum in fundraising, with $37 billion raised in the quarter, driving a total of $122 billion in fundraising for the year-to-date, reflecting investor demand for experienced investment managers. Considering the strength, we now expect full year fundraising of roughly $150 billion. Given the sustained levels of investment performance for clients, our leading asset and wealth management business remains very well positioned for continued growth amid attractive secular tailwinds. At the same time, we are also inorganically accelerating growth and building a stronger platform with a better product offering for clients. In August, we announced agreements to acquire NEOS, a market leader in derivative income ETFs with approximately $35 billion in AUM at quarter end, and LCN Capital Partners, a leading triple net lease investment manager. The NEOS acquisition would bring our global active ETF assets under supervision to over $90 billion, establishing Goldman Sachs among the top eight providers by assets under supervision and top six by revenue. While LCN broadens the range of private real estate investment solutions we can offer. Importantly, these acquisitions also bring talented and entrepreneurial teams to Goldman Sachs. We remain focused on opportunities that enhance distribution, deepen investment capabilities, and add products to strengthen asset and wealth management. Our bar for strategic financial and cultural fit remains very high, and we will continue to allocate capital dynamically and with discipline as we drive growth. All in, our record year-to-date revenues are the result of years of focused execution that have strengthened our market-leading businesses and increased connectivity across the firm as we harnessed the power of One Goldman Sachs. Importantly, we have created a higher revenue base with our more durable revenues having more than doubled since 2020 Investor Day, and now representing approximately 45% of revenues for the year-to-date. The increased durability, coupled with our expense discipline and prudent capital management, enhances the resilience of our earnings and supports higher returns through the cycle, providing Goldman Sachs with an even stronger foundation for growth. Looking forward, though uncertainty persists, corporates and investors recognize that standing still can be a competitive disadvantage. Clients are taking action to modernize operations, secure critical capabilities, and reallocate capital towards their highest return opportunities. All of this is driving demand for M&A, capital formation, financing, risk management, and advice, playing directly to the strength of our franchise. An ongoing theme has been the growth in AI infrastructure investment. Recent studies estimate that the U.S. data center build-out could require north of $10 trillion in investment through 2032, averaging roughly 3.6% of U.S. GDP annually. In our conversations with clients, demand for compute significantly exceeds supply at the moment, creating opportunities to help develop financing structures to meet that capacity shortfall. Our differentiated financing, distribution, and investing capabilities position us to play a meaningful role in the mobilization of capital and supporting client activity. While we are proud of the privileged position we play in the AI investment cycle, no one knows how the demands for capital and compute will evolve as the broader AI ecosystem matures. That will only become clearer as technology and markets continue to develop. This uncertainty reinforces the importance of remaining vigilant around the types of activity we finance and how we manage risk as we support our clients. We are highly selective about the risk we underwrite and the capital we commit, particularly as client financing needs become larger and more complex. Beyond these financial risks, we also recognize the broader concerns around the accelerating pace of AI technology and the unchecked advancement of frontier models. Like other transformative technologies, AI presents significant opportunities, but also significant risks that must be carefully assessed and managed. However, the choice is not between halting progress and moving forward without guardrails. We must enable innovation and also demand responsibility. The experience of the financial services industry has demonstrated the value of rigorous testing, independent review and continuous monitoring, and clear human accountability. These principles, applied in ways that reflect the unique characteristics of AI, can help build the trust and confidence needed to deploy the technology responsibly at scale while companies, developers, and governments work together to establish appropriate safeguards. All in, we continue to see meaningful opportunities ahead of us. We are incredibly well positioned given our relentless focus on serving our clients while remaining vigilant to emerging risks in this dynamic environment. Our culture of teamwork, excellence, and partnership remains a key differentiator that has enabled us to adapt, innovate, and execute through a range of environments. I've never been more confident in our ability to create long-term value for shareholders by making the right investments to grow the firm and generate sustainable earnings growth. With that, I'll turn it over to Denis to walk through our financial results in more detail. Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. Let's start with our results on page one of the presentation. In the third quarter, we generated net revenues of $18.7 billion, earnings per share of $17.01, which drove a quarterly ROE of 18.7% and ROTE of 20.5%. Turning to segment performance starting on page three. Global banking and markets revenues were $13.5 billion in the third quarter, our second highest quarterly revenues, contributing to a segment ROE of 23.5% for the year-to-date. Moving to page four, advisory revenues of $1.7 billion reached a quarterly record and rose 18% year-over-year, driven by higher volumes. For the year-to-date, we maintained our number one league table position for announced and completed M&A volumes. In equity underwriting, revenues of $666 million rose 43% year-over-year on strong IPO and secondary offerings activity. In debt underwriting, revenues were $904 million, up 15% year-over-year, driven primarily by stronger investment grade activity. year-to-date, we ranked number one in equity underwriting, number two in leveraged loans, and number three in high yield debt underwriting. Even amid very strong accruals in the quarter, our investment banking backlog remains very robust, as strong revenue realizations and advisory were largely offset by solid replenishment and equity underwriting. year-to-date, sponsor share of announced M&A remains below historical averages, presenting further upside when activity picks up. FICC net revenues were essentially unchanged year-over-year. Intermediation revenues declined 7%, as lower results in mortgages, rates, and credit were largely offset by strong performance in currencies and commodities. Financing revenues increased 14% to their second highest level, driven by strength in mortgages and structured financing. Equities net revenues were $6.4 billion, up 72% year-over-year, representing our second-best quarter, driven by strong performance in both intermediation and financing. Equities intermediation revenues rose 52% to their second highest level, driven by strength in derivatives. Equities financing revenues rose 96% to a record driven primarily by elevated average prime balances and strong activity across Asia. Demand for equities financing continues to exceed available industry capacity, supporting attractive pricing and allowing us to remain selective in deploying resources. Following significant multi-year investment, our focus is increasingly on optimizing a diversified global portfolio, guided by our risk management framework, client relationships, and returns. More broadly, we continue to see structural tailwinds for the growth in tradable assets and the increasing financing needs associated with those assets, which have helped to support sustained industry growth and equities financing over time. Year-to-date, total financing revenues of $12.7 billion were a record and represented over 40% of combined FICC and equities revenues. As David mentioned, growth in financing revenues has contributed to greater durability in FICC and equities, and is underpinned by a robust risk framework that includes diversified exposures, limits, concentration management, and comprehensive stress testing. Let's turn to page five. Asset and wealth management revenues were $5.1 billion, up 14% year-over-year. Management and other fees rose 22% year-over-year to a record $3.6 billion, reflecting the impact of higher average assets under supervision. Incentive fees were $587 million. Through our ultra high net worth wealth management franchise, we provided clients early access to a high growth investment opportunity and recognized incentive fees following the company's IPO. Based on our current outlook, we expect incentive fees to remain elevated in the fourth quarter. Private banking and lending revenues were $827 million, up 20% sequentially, driven by higher net interest from consumer deposits. Loan balances were up 6% to $51 billion. Investments revenues were $50 million, given the timing of certain monetizations following a strong second quarter and certain markdowns. Now moving to page six. Total assets under supervision ended the quarter at a record $4.1 trillion, supported by $97 billion of long-term fee-based net inflows, marking our 35th consecutive quarter of long-term fee-based net inflows. Wealth management client assets reached another record of $2.1 trillion, with $47 billion of long-term net inflows. Turning to page seven. Alternative assets under supervision totaled $491 billion at the end of the third quarter, driving $860 million in management and other fees, the best performance since our 2020 Investor Day. Gross third-party alternatives fundraising was $37 billion for the quarter and $122 billion for the year-to-date. On page nine, firm wide net interest income was $3.8 billion. Our total loan portfolio increased 6% from the prior quarter to $276 billion, reflecting broad-based growth across the portfolio. Our provision for credit losses was $368 million. While overall credit quality and portfolio performance have remained strong, our provisions reflected certain impairments across our portfolio as well as overall growth in lending. Turning to expenses on page 10. Total operating expenses were $11.3 billion for the quarter. For the year-to-date, total operating expenses were $33.4 billion for an efficiency ratio of 59.4%, improving 270 basis points from the prior year and in line with our target. That is generally considered a lower comp ratio business. Has it been like business mix that has helped the comp ratio, or are you just seeing lower competition for talent? Thanks for taking my questions. Sure. I would say there are a couple of things in terms of how we think about the comp ratio. First, it is our best estimate at the moment for what we expect for the year, but I would say that we are applying a strategic lens to it, and your question does get after this. As we look at ways that we can invest to grow the firm, grow the earnings of the firm, scale the firm, we are building durable platform-connected types of businesses, and over time, we should not have the same degree of headcount-related expenses that we might have historically to grow and scale the firm. Certain of the more durable activities, including the financing activities, we are using a lot of the firm's financial resources and risk appetite to drive that activity. There can be favorable compensation ratio benefits with respect to the growth of those activities. I would not say that we're seeing any diminution in terms of the market for talent. Frankly, quite the opposite. I think for the very, very best people in this environment, business professionals, engineering professionals across the firm, there's a very, very strong bid for the very, very best people, and we make sure that we're in a position to compensate them appropriately. But we are focused over the longer term on sustainably delivering operating leverage to our shareholders as we grow the firm. This is one step in that direction. We will take our next question from Dan Fannon with Jefferies. Thanks. Good morning. So one more on expenses, Denis, and shifting to non-comp, obviously excluding the charitable numbers in this quarter and I think next quarter, as you highlighted. Could you just talk about the growth rate or outlook for non-comp expense as you think about the AI benefits you might be seeing in other areas investment that could be growing or shrinking as we look ahead? Sure. First and foremost, you can see it in the numbers, both aggregate and the deltas. By far, the biggest component is transaction-based expenses. That story remains the same. For so long as we continue to see strong levels of client activity, particularly in equities and particularly in Asia, we'd expect that we'll continue to see growth in the transaction-based expenses. You're right. By the end of this year, based on our current expectations, we'll have made contributions to support go-forward charitable giving that hopefully should carry us through about five years or so on our best estimate. So you're unlikely to see that in the future periods as a result. The other area of strategic growth is across technology, generally speaking, in comms and tech. We're going to continue to make sure that our people have access to the cutting-edge technology. We're making investments in our data infrastructure, our migrations to cloud. We're obviously making investments with respect to the models. We're also making talent investments, all to make sure that we can support the firm's scaled growth over time. I would call those out as the areas of focus. Understood. Just as a follow-up, wealth management organic growth more than accelerated, $47 billion in the quarter in terms of net inflows. Anything one time in there or chunky that you would call out or maybe just talk to the components, whether it was new advisor adds, recruiting, same store sales with existing clients, what was the driver there? I would not call out a particular one time. I would say that we have now a multi-year sustained investment in expanding our advisor footprint. That's a decision that was made a number of years ago. We continue to ramp up. Advisors continue to expand our geographic footprint and our reach around the world. We continue to have very, very strong investment performance, which is really important. We continue to invest in the overall quality of our people and in terms of the client experience that our clients have with our people. It's a big area of strategic focus for the firm. It is performing substantially ahead of the targets that we put out earlier this year of 5%, but we're very pleased, and it's a huge opportunity for the firm. We will take our next question from Devin Ryan with Citizens Bank. Thanks. Good morning, David and Denis. A couple here on asset management, and really on the alts business. It's just been incredibly impressive fundraising. You started the year at a $75 billion-$100 billion target. Now you're kind of targeting $150 billion. Clearly a lot of incremental capital coming in here. Just curious if you could give us a little more color around how much of that is just being kind of opportunistic in the market with some of these themes, like the volatility in private credit, or whether there's something maybe bigger structurally that's been changing around your ability to distribute or even add capacity to that business. Yeah. I appreciate the question, Devin, but there's nothing opportunistic about it. This is a concerted strategy that started six-plus years ago to really scale the platform. When you look across the platform, it's a scaled platform. We've got managers across a variety of the different categories of private capital raising that have a lot of experience, good performance. We've been very, very good to institutional allocators at customizing solutions that work for them with a long-term view. In addition, we have very, very good demand for these products and services from our ultra-high net worth channel, which is a very, very important component. This has been a strategic decision that we've made real scaled progress on over a period of time that has meaningfully increased our capacity to compete at the highest level in the space. I think we've got good runway. When you look at private credit, for example, one of the things we've benefited from is we've been in this business for 40 years. Institutional allocators, despite the noise in the media around private credit, as spreads have normalized to more attractive levels, institutional allocators have thought this is a more attractive time in the last three to six months to bring capital into experienced private credit managers, and we've benefited from that. There's nothing opportunistic. This is a long-term strategy to have one of the largest and broadest private alts platforms, and you're seeing the benefit of our scaled position start to come through. Appreciate that, David. Just a follow-up just on the acquisition front in asset management. Clearly, it's been an area of doing ETFs. Are there any other areas you feel like you're still sub-scale in asset management, or where a few additional capabilities or investments could kind of, like you just said on the alt side, similarly really kind of improve the capacity or make you more relevant with institutional or retail clients? Thanks. Yeah. There's no question. We still have gaps across the platform. We have a presence across all the variety of private assets broadly, but there's some places where we're not as scaled as we'd like to be. That doesn't mean that we'll make an acquisition in that space because there's got to be fit, there's got to be the right team. But we continue to look for places where we're not scaled, where there are opportunities, both across privates and the public side of our asset management business to increase our scale. I think there'll be other opportunities. I'm not going to call out something specifically. But we're not at scale everywhere, and if we see an opportunity that fits and accelerates our scale position, we're certainly going to consider it. But always with a very high bar around culture fit and the specific people we're bringing into the firm. Thank you. We'll take our next question from Gerard Cassidy with RBC. Hi, David. Hi, Denis. Denis, you touched on in your comments about the provision being higher, that you gave us guidance earlier in the quarter about it being higher. So there's no real surprise. The outlook for credit from your comments still is strong. But can you elaborate a little bit on the marks that you took to drove that provision? Sure. There's two drivers this quarter that are worth taking note of. One, which is the secondary driver, but yet it's important, which is overall growth in the portfolio. We continue to deploy capital to expand the opportunities to lend to more clients. And frankly, that's an outgrowth of a strategic decision earlier in the year when we found ourselves with more excess capital that we wanted to fuel growth in our overall investment banking coverage suite of relationships. So a component of the provision number is aggregate growth in the portfolio. But it is the case as well that the impairment numbers were elevated. We looked very carefully, as we always do, at the entire complexion of the portfolio. Our conclusion is they're a highly idiosyncratic to non-correlated set of names, but we had a couple of different names that we ended up taking incremental impairments against in the quarter. We don't think it's necessarily the signal of something else to come. But it was appropriate for those individual names, and so we took the impairments and put it through in the third quarter. Very good. Then as a follow-up, you talked about it earlier in the year about the leaning into Asia and the success that you've had, and you touched on it again today, the Asian markets and the equity financing when the execution, you guys obviously benefit from. Are there any other opportunities globally where you can lean into new markets and get the benefits that you're seeing similar to what you did with Asia? I think there are opportunities all over the world where we can continue to lean in. What we found particularly attractive about Asia is that we felt that we were quite under scale, and the opportunity was available with clients on attractive economic and risk terms. And so it was the most attractive place geographically to drive incremental penetration and scale, and that's why we made it a priority. But there are plenty of other places around the world that we could continue to choose to drive incremental growth as well. Thank you. We'll take our next question from Chris McGratty with KBW. Oh, great. Thanks for squeezing me in. David, more of a high-level question. Your outperformance on your ROE to targets, maybe a comment or two on your views on how much is cyclical versus structural. I appreciate the question, Chris. I think a lot of it is we're structurally running the firm as a broader, more durable franchise with higher fundamental returns. I'm not going to speculate on through the cycle as to how the returns balanced out. But what I will say when I go back over the last five years, I remember sitting on this call for multiple years, including as recently as a couple of years ago, when we were very confident that we could get the firm running through our targets through the cycle, and there was a lot of skepticism about that. The reason the returns are significantly elevated is because we've significantly grown the breadth and the base of the firm. We've significantly changed the operational structure and the durability of the firm, and that's led to higher structural returns. There's a big strategic result of an investment over a long period of time. I will say, at the moment, and I've said it on the call three times, we're in a very good environment. We're in a top quartile environment. Does that flatter what will be the average returns through the cycle? Absolutely. But structurally, the base returns of the firm have been meaningfully uplifted over the last five years. Perfect. Then second follow-up would be the midterms. I think there's a divided view of whether a divided government is good for activity or perhaps a headwind. Where do you stand on if the futures markets are right about a divided government, how that could play into your capital markets business? Thanks. First of all, the election doesn't occur for another month, and in politics, a month is an eternity, so we'll see how the election plays out. I'm not a good pundit, nor are the prediction markets or the futures markets a good pundit of exactly what the environment will bring after the election as we head into 2027. So, we'll watch that and be prepared for whatever comes our way. Thank you. At this time, there are no additional questions. Ladies and gentlemen, this concludes The Goldman Sachs Group third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect. Goldman Sachs delivered record year-to-date revenues and robust Q3 results, with net revenues of $18.7B (second highest ever), EPS of $17.01, and ROE of 18.7%. Asset and wealth management, alternatives fundraising, and capital markets activity were standouts, with management raising full-year alternatives fundraising guidance to $150B and highlighting continued strong client demand despite a complex macro environment. Good morning. My name is [Katie] and I will be your conference facilitator today. I would like to welcome everyone to The Goldman Sachs third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. On behalf of Goldman Sachs, I will begin the call with the following disclaimer. The earnings presentation can be found on the investor relations page of the goldmansachs.com website and contains information on forward-looking statements and non-GAAP measures. This audiocast is copyrighted material of The Goldman Sachs Group Inc., and may not be duplicated, reproduced, or rebroadcast without consent. This call is being recorded today, October 13, 2026. I will now turn the call over to Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, David Solomon, and Chief Financial Officer, Denis Coleman. Thank you. Mr. Solomon, you may begin your conference. Thank you, operator. Good morning, everybody. Thank you for joining us. We delivered very strong performance in the third quarter, generating net revenues of $18.7 billion, the second highest in our history, earnings per share of $17.01, an ROE of 18.7%, and an ROTE of 20.5%. Our quarterly results included the impact of an accelerated charitable contribution. Excluding that contribution, quarterly EPS would've been approximately $18, and ROE and ROTE would've been approximately 20% and 21.5% respectively. For the year-to-date, we delivered record revenues driving an ROE of 20.7% and an ROTE of 22.4%. While the third quarter began with optimism around a potential resolution of the conflict in the Middle East, renewed geopolitical tensions and continued disruption of energy flows added complexity to the outlook, increasing oil prices, reigniting inflation concerns, and driving bond yields higher. Against this backdrop, the Fed raised rates in September for the first time in three years, with markets pricing in approximately 75 basis points of additional tightening in this cycle across the U.S., U.K., and Europe. Despite these crosscurrents, the health of the underlying U.S. economy has remained solid, with strong corporate earnings growth, GDP growth of 2.2%, and a very resilient labor market. In complex environments such as these, clients rely on the advice, execution, and intermediation expertise of Goldman Sachs to navigate uncertainty and advance their most important strategic priorities. In global banking and markets, we generated the second highest revenues in our history. Within investment banking, advisory revenues were a record, and we maintained our longstanding number one position in M&A, advising on $1.5 trillion of announced transactions for the year. We maintained our year-to-date lead over our closest peer of approximately $430 billion, the largest lead we've ever had, as clients turn to us for advice on significant transactions, including Hugging Face's $13 billion sale to NVIDIA and Integer Holdings' $6 billion sale to KKR. As you'll remember, we entered the quarter with our highest backlog in five years, and even with exceptionally strong revenue production in the quarter, our backlog remains very robust, reflecting the strength and breadth of client engagement across our leading investment banking franchise. In equities, we delivered our second-best performance after last quarter's record results, with strength across both intermediation and financing. In FICC, we remain steadfast in supporting our clients' global risk intermediation needs across asset classes amid sharp moves in rates and increased volatility in commodities. Importantly, financing activities have become a larger and more durable component of our markets businesses, representing over 40% of FICC and equities revenues year-to-date. This progress reflects strong client demand, prudent balance sheet deployment, and continued execution against our strategic priorities, including deliberate multi-year investments in Asia, which we highlighted earlier this year as an opportunity to drive further share gains. This dynamic market backdrop has also reinforced the importance of trusted advice and diversified investment solutions for asset and wealth management clients. Our scaled and durable platform brings together leading investment capabilities across public and private markets and delivers them through deep institutional relationships, our ultra-premier high net worth wealth management franchise, and our expanding third-party distribution network. The strength of this platform continues to drive exceptional growth at scale. In the third quarter, management and other fees increased 22% year-over-year to a record $3.6 billion and surpassed $10 billion for the year-to-date. Our assets under supervision reached another record of $4.1 trillion, supported by $97 billion of long-term net inflows, representing our 35th consecutive quarter of inflows. In wealth management, $47 billion of long-term net inflows contributed to record client assets of $2.1 trillion. For 2026, wealth management long-term net inflows are annualizing at 12%, well ahead of our 5% target, which underscores the strength of our client relationships built on trust and long-term performance. In alternatives, we are driving strong growth, with alternative assets under supervision up 26% year-over-year to a record $491 billion. We continue to see strong momentum in fundraising, with $37 billion raised in the quarter, driving a total of $122 billion in fundraising for the year-to-date, reflecting investor demand for experienced investment managers. Considering the strength, we now expect full year fundraising of roughly $150 billion. Given the sustained levels of investment performance for clients, our leading asset and wealth management business remains very well positioned for continued growth amid attractive secular tailwinds. At the same time, we are also inorganically accelerating growth and building a stronger platform with a better product offering for clients. In August, we announced agreements to acquire NEOS, a market leader in derivative income ETFs with approximately $35 billion in AUM at quarter end, and LCN Capital Partners, a leading triple net lease investment manager. The NEOS acquisition would bring our global active ETF assets under supervision to over $90 billion, establishing Goldman Sachs among the top eight providers by assets under supervision and top six by revenue. While LCN broadens the range of private real estate investment solutions we can offer. Importantly, these acquisitions also bring talented and entrepreneurial teams to Goldman Sachs. We remain focused on opportunities that enhance distribution, deepen investment capabilities, and add products to strengthen asset and wealth management. Our bar for strategic financial and cultural fit remains very high, and we will continue to allocate capital dynamically and with discipline as we drive growth. All in, our record year-to-date revenues are the result of years of focused execution that have strengthened our market-leading businesses and increased connectivity across the firm as we harnessed the power of One Goldman Sachs. Importantly, we have created a higher revenue base with our more durable revenues having more than doubled since 2020 Investor Day, and now representing approximately 45% of revenues for the year-to-date. The increased durability, coupled with our expense discipline and prudent capital management, enhances the resilience of our earnings and supports higher returns through the cycle, providing Goldman Sachs with an even stronger foundation for growth. Looking forward, though uncertainty persists, corporates and investors recognize that standing still can be a competitive disadvantage. Clients are taking action to modernize operations, secure critical capabilities, and reallocate capital towards their highest return opportunities. All of this is driving demand for M&A, capital formation, financing, risk management, and advice, playing directly to the strength of our franchise. An ongoing theme has been the growth in AI infrastructure investment. Recent studies estimate that the U.S. data center build-out could require north of $10 trillion in investment through 2032, averaging roughly 3.6% of U.S. GDP annually. In our conversations with clients, demand for compute significantly exceeds supply at the moment, creating opportunities to help develop financing structures to meet that capacity shortfall. Our differentiated financing, distribution, and investing capabilities position us to play a meaningful role in the mobilization of capital and supporting client activity. While we are proud of the privileged position we play in the AI investment cycle, no one knows how the demands for capital and compute will evolve as the broader AI ecosystem matures. That will only become clearer as technology and markets continue to develop. This uncertainty reinforces the importance of remaining vigilant around the types of activity we finance and how we manage risk as we support our clients. We are highly selective about the risk we underwrite and the capital we commit, particularly as client financing needs become larger and more complex. Beyond these financial risks, we also recognize the broader concerns around the accelerating pace of AI technology and the unchecked advancement of frontier models. Like other transformative technologies, AI presents significant opportunities, but also significant risks that must be carefully assessed and managed. However, the choice is not between halting progress and moving forward without guardrails. We must enable innovation and also demand responsibility. The experience of the financial services industry has demonstrated the value of rigorous testing, independent review and continuous monitoring, and clear human accountability. These principles, applied in ways that reflect the unique characteristics of AI, can help build the trust and confidence needed to deploy the technology responsibly at scale while companies, developers, and governments work together to establish appropriate safeguards. All in, we continue to see meaningful opportunities ahead of us. We are incredibly well positioned given our relentless focus on serving our clients while remaining vigilant to emerging risks in this dynamic environment. Our culture of teamwork, excellence, and partnership remains a key differentiator that has enabled us to adapt, innovate, and execute through a range of environments. I've never been more confident in our ability to create long-term value for shareholders by making the right investments to grow the firm and generate sustainable earnings growth. With that, I'll turn it over to Denis to walk through our financial results in more detail. Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. Let's start with our results on page one of the presentation. In the third quarter, we generated net revenues of $18.7 billion, earnings per share of $17.01, which drove a quarterly ROE of 18.7% and ROTE of 20.5%. Turning to segment performance starting on page three. Global banking and markets revenues were $13.5 billion in the third quarter, our second highest quarterly revenues, contributing to a segment ROE of 23.5% for the year-to-date. Moving to page four, advisory revenues of $1.7 billion reached a quarterly record and rose 18% year-over-year, driven by higher volumes. For the year-to-date, we maintained our number one league table position for announced and completed M&A volumes. In equity underwriting, revenues of $666 million rose 43% year-over-year on strong IPO and secondary offerings activity. In debt underwriting, revenues were $904 million, up 15% year-over-year, driven primarily by stronger investment grade activity. year-to-date, we ranked number one in equity underwriting, number two in leveraged loans, and number three in high yield debt underwriting. Even amid very strong accruals in the quarter, our investment banking backlog remains very robust, as strong revenue realizations and advisory were largely offset by solid replenishment and equity underwriting. year-to-date, sponsor share of announced M&A remains below historical averages, presenting further upside when activity picks up. FICC net revenues were essentially unchanged year-over-year. Intermediation revenues declined 7%, as lower results in mortgages, rates, and credit were largely offset by strong performance in currencies and commodities. Financing revenues increased 14% to their second highest level, driven by strength in mortgages and structured financing. Equities net revenues were $6.4 billion, up 72% year-over-year, representing our second-best quarter, driven by strong performance in both intermediation and financing. Equities intermediation revenues rose 52% to their second highest level, driven by strength in derivatives. Equities financing revenues rose 96% to a record driven primarily by elevated average prime balances and strong activity across Asia. Demand for equities financing continues to exceed available industry capacity, supporting attractive pricing and allowing us to remain selective in deploying resources. Following significant multi-year investment, our focus is increasingly on optimizing a diversified global portfolio, guided by our risk management framework, client relationships, and returns. More broadly, we continue to see structural tailwinds for the growth in tradable assets and the increasing financing needs associated with those assets, which have helped to support sustained industry growth and equities financing over time. Year-to-date, total financing revenues of $12.7 billion were a record and represented over 40% of combined FICC and equities revenues. As David mentioned, growth in financing revenues has contributed to greater durability in FICC and equities, and is underpinned by a robust risk framework that includes diversified exposures, limits, concentration management, and comprehensive stress testing. Let's turn to page five. Asset and wealth management revenues were $5.1 billion, up 14% year-over-year. Management and other fees rose 22% year-over-year to a record $3.6 billion, reflecting the impact of higher average assets under supervision. Incentive fees were $587 million. Through our ultra high net worth wealth management franchise, we provided clients early access to a high growth investment opportunity and recognized incentive fees following the company's IPO. Based on our current outlook, we expect incentive fees to remain elevated in the fourth quarter. Private banking and lending revenues were $827 million, up 20% sequentially, driven by higher net interest from consumer deposits. Loan balances were up 6% to $51 billion. Investments revenues were $50 million, given the timing of certain monetizations following a strong second quarter and certain markdowns. Now moving to page six. Total assets under supervision ended the quarter at a record $4.1 trillion, supported by $97 billion of long-term fee-based net inflows, marking our 35th consecutive quarter of long-term fee-based net inflows. Wealth management client assets reached another record of $2.1 trillion, with $47 billion of long-term net inflows. Turning to page seven. Alternative assets under supervision totaled $491 billion at the end of the third quarter, driving $860 million in management and other fees, the best performance since our 2020 Investor Day. Gross third-party alternatives fundraising was $37 billion for the quarter and $122 billion for the year-to-date. On page nine, firm wide net interest income was $3.8 billion. Our total loan portfolio increased 6% from the prior quarter to $276 billion, reflecting broad-based growth across the portfolio. Our provision for credit losses was $368 million. While overall credit quality and portfolio performance have remained strong, our provisions reflected certain impairments across our portfolio as well as overall growth in lending. Turning to expenses on page 10. Total operating expenses were $11.3 billion for the quarter. For the year-to-date, total operating expenses were $33.4 billion for an efficiency ratio of 59.4%, improving 270 basis points from the prior year and in line with our target. Our year-to-date compensation ratio net of provisions was reduced to 30%. We remain committed to paying for performance and delivering operating leverage for shareholders. Quarterly non-compensation expenses were $6.2 billion, 30% higher year-over-year, driven largely by higher transaction-based expenses. Additionally, given the strong pull-through of incentive fees this quarter, we made a tax efficient charitable contribution of approximately $450 million as part of a planned acceleration of our philanthropic efforts. We also expect to make a meaningful contribution in the fourth quarter. Together, these actions will pull forward at least five years of planned charitable giving. The impact of our charitable contributions on quarterly EPS was approximately $1, while the impact on ROE and ROTE was approximately 1.1 percentage points each. Our effective tax rate for the year-to-date was 20.4%, and for the full year, we continue to expect an effective tax rate of approximately 20%. Now on to slide 11. Our common equity Tier One ratio was 12.4% at the end of the third quarter under the standardized approach, 100 basis points above our current capital requirement of 11.4%. Regarding recent regulatory developments, we welcome the Federal Reserve's rule finalization to enhance the transparency and accountability of the CCAR stress test and reduce the volatility of capital requirements. We also recognize the progress of the Basel III endgame and G-SIB surcharge proposals and are hopeful for finalization by the end of the year. Collectively, these developments represent meaningful progress towards a more balanced and risk-sensitive regulatory capital framework that preserves the strength and resilience of the banking system. As the rules are finalized, we support appropriately calibrated requirements that are aligned with the risks firms actually take and look forward to the timely completion of these reforms. We expect regulatory focus to soon shift towards liquidity regulation reform. We currently have over $570 billion in average global core liquid assets, representing approximately 25% of our total assets, and our liquidity coverage ratio is among the highest in our peer group. In the quarter, we repurchased $3 billion of our common stock and paid $1.5 billion in dividends. We continue to have significant capacity to deploy capital prudently in service of clients while maintaining an appropriate buffer. In conclusion, our third quarter performance reflects the strength of our client franchise, which has been bolstered by years of strategic execution. We've built market-leading franchises, deep relationships, and a higher and more durable revenue base. We remain focused on delivering strong returns while continuing to invest in our people, technology, and client franchises to drive long-term earnings growth and deliver for our shareholders. With that, we'll now open up the line for questions. Thank you. Please stand by as we assemble our queue. If you would like to ask a question during this time, simply press star then the number one on your telephone keypad. If you would like to withdraw your question, press star then two on your telephone keypad. If you're asking a question and are on a hands-free unit or a speakerphone, we would like to ask that you use your handset when asking your question. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up question. We'll take our first question from Glenn Schorr with Evercore ISI. Hi there. Thank you. First one on trading and markets. The results are nothing short of awesome. There's a short-term and long-term question I have. The short term is just simple. Is there anything unique in the quarter like related situational awareness or anything like that would contribute to the quarter such that we don't over model in the fourth quarter? The bigger picture question I want to ask you is, there's so many developments going on, tokenization, agentic trading, DeFi vaults, prediction markets. We continue to ramp up. Advisors continue to expand our geographic footprint and our reach around the world. We continue to have very, very strong investment performance, which is really important. We continue to invest in the overall quality of our people and in terms of the client experience that our clients have with our people. It's a big area of strategic focus for the firm. It is performing substantially ahead of the targets that we put out earlier this year of 5%, but we're very pleased, and it's a huge opportunity for the firm. We will take our next question from Devin Ryan with Citizens Bank. Thanks. Good morning, David and Denis. A couple here on asset management, and really on the alts business. It's just been incredibly impressive fundraising. You started the year at a $75 billion-$100 billion target. Now you're kind of targeting $150 billion. Clearly a lot of incremental capital coming in here. Just curious if you could give us a little more color around how much of that is just being kind of opportunistic in the market with some of these themes, like the volatility in private credit, or whether there's something maybe bigger structurally that's been changing around your ability to distribute or even add capacity to that business. Yeah. I appreciate the question, Devin, but there's nothing opportunistic about it. This is a concerted strategy that started six-plus years ago to really scale the platform. When you look across the platform, it's a scaled platform. We've got managers across a variety of the different categories of private capital raising that have a lot of experience, good performance. We've been very, very good to institutional allocators at customizing solutions that work for them with a long-term view. In addition, we have very, very good demand for these products and services from our ultra-high net worth channel, which is a very, very important component. This has been a strategic decision that we've made real scaled progress on over a period of time that has meaningfully increased our capacity to compete at the highest level in the space. I think we've got good runway. When you look at private credit, for example, one of the things we've benefited from is we've been in this business for 40 years. Institutional allocators, despite the noise in the media around private credit, as spreads have normalized to more attractive levels, institutional allocators have thought this is a more attractive time in the last three to six months to bring capital into experienced private credit managers, and we've benefited from that. There's nothing opportunistic. This is a long-term strategy to have one of the largest and broadest private alts platforms, and you're seeing the benefit of our scaled position start to come through. Appreciate that, David. Just a follow-up just on the acquisition front in asset management. Clearly, it's been an area of doing ETFs. Are there any other areas you feel like you're still sub-scale in asset management, or where a few additional capabilities or investments could kind of, like you just said on the alt side, similarly really kind of improve the capacity or make you more relevant with institutional or retail clients? Thanks. Yeah. There's no question. We still have gaps across the platform. We have a presence across all the variety of private assets broadly, but there's some places where we're not as scaled as we'd like to be. That doesn't mean that we'll make an acquisition in that space because there's got to be fit, there's got to be the right team. But we continue to look for places where we're not scaled, where there are opportunities, both across privates and the public side of our asset management business to increase our scale. I think there'll be other opportunities. I'm not going to call out something specifically. But we're not at scale everywhere, and if we see an opportunity that fits and accelerates our scale position, we're certainly going to consider it. But always with a very high bar around culture fit and the specific people we're bringing into the firm. Thank you. We'll take our next question from Gerard Cassidy with RBC. Hi, David. Hi, Denis. Denis, you touched on in your comments about the provision being higher, that you gave us guidance earlier in the quarter about it being higher. So there's no real surprise. The outlook for credit from your comments still is strong. But can you elaborate a little bit on the marks that you took to drove that provision? Sure. There's two drivers this quarter that are worth taking note of. One, which is the secondary driver, but yet it's important, which is overall growth in the portfolio. We continue to deploy capital to expand the opportunities to lend to more clients. And frankly, that's an outgrowth of a strategic decision earlier in the year when we found ourselves with more excess capital that we wanted to fuel growth in our overall investment banking coverage suite of relationships. So a component of the provision number is aggregate growth in the portfolio. But it is the case as well that the impairment numbers were elevated. We looked very carefully, as we always do, at the entire complexion of the portfolio. Our conclusion is they're a highly idiosyncratic to non-correlated set of names, but we had a couple of different names that we ended up taking incremental impairments against in the quarter. We don't think it's necessarily the signal of something else to come. But it was appropriate for those individual names, and so we took the impairments and put it through in the third quarter. Very good. Then as a follow-up, you talked about it earlier in the year about the leaning into Asia and the success that you've had, and you touched on it again today, the Asian markets and the equity financing when the execution, you guys obviously benefit from. Are there any other opportunities globally where you can lean into new markets and get the benefits that you're seeing similar to what you did with Asia? I think there are opportunities all over the world where we can continue to lean in. What we found particularly attractive about Asia is that we felt that we were quite under scale, and the opportunity was available with clients on attractive economic and risk terms. And so it was the most attractive place geographically to drive incremental penetration and scale, and that's why we made it a priority. But there are plenty of other places around the world that we could continue to choose to drive incremental growth as well. Thank you. We'll take our next question from Chris McGratty with KBW. Oh, great. Thanks for squeezing me in. David, more of a high-level question. Your outperformance on your ROE to targets, maybe a comment or two on your views on how much is cyclical versus structural. I appreciate the question, Chris. I think a lot of it is we're structurally running the firm as a broader, more durable franchise with higher fundamental returns. I'm not going to speculate on through the cycle as to how the returns balanced out. But what I will say when I go back over the last five years, I remember sitting on this call for multiple years, including as recently as a couple of years ago, when we were very confident that we could get the firm running through our targets through the cycle, and there was a lot of skepticism about that. The reason the returns are significantly elevated is because we've significantly grown the breadth and the base of the firm. We've significantly changed the operational structure and the durability of the firm, and that's led to higher structural returns. There's a big strategic result of an investment over a long period of time. I will say, at the moment, and I've said it on the call three times, we're in a very good environment. We're in a top quartile environment. Does that flatter what will be the average returns through the cycle? Absolutely. But structurally, the base returns of the firm have been meaningfully uplifted over the last five years. Perfect. Then second follow-up would be the midterms. I think there's a divided view of whether a divided government is good for activity or perhaps a headwind. Where do you stand on if the futures markets are right about a divided government, how that could play into your capital markets business? Thanks. First of all, the election doesn't occur for another month, and in politics, a month is an eternity, so we'll see how the election plays out. I'm not a good pundit, nor are the prediction markets or the futures markets a good pundit of exactly what the environment will bring after the election as we head into 2027. So, we'll watch that and be prepared for whatever comes our way. Thank you. At this time, there are no additional questions. title: Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (The) (GS-PC) Q3 FY2026 earnings call transcript - Yahoo Finance
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results Goldman Sachs delivered record year-to-date revenues and robust Q3 results, with net revenues of $18.7B (second highest ever), EPS of $17.01, and ROE of 18.7%.
